title: Fragrance from Sickly Bones: The Dandy Husband Can't Keep Up the Act
author: Mo Liao
synopsis:
[Main story completed] Both leads pure and untainted, HE
[Calculating profligate & secret crush turned reality × Languid, sickly beauty × Pampering his wife to extremes]

Wen Qionghua, the sole legitimate daughter of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate in three generations, was stunningly peerless in beauty, yet born frail and sickly.

Betrothed to the aloof Buddhist-like Xie Linfeng, he publicly humiliated her for the sake of a noodle-selling maiden.

She wearily lifted her gaze: "Let's call off the engagement."

Until Xie Linyuan, the devastatingly handsome and "profligate" eldest illegitimate son of the Xie family, pinned her against the wall in public, his fingertips tracing her pale lips:
"Jiaojia, look at me... am I worthy?"
Later on, Xie Linfeng knelt outside the courtyard with red eyes, begging to reconcile.

Meanwhile, she was trapped on the couch by that "profligate," his gaze dangerous yet deeply affectionate:
"Jiaojia, indulge your husband a little more, won't you?..."

"Weren't you just..."

"Wife is too breathtaking, this husband... hasn't had enough..."

(Male lead plays the profligate while secretly possessing layer upon layer of formidable hidden identities + Female lead is a sickly beauty with a dark lotus core, extreme push-and-pull sweet romance!)

chapters.title: Fragrance Rises from Sickly Bones
chapters.content:
Pain~

A pair of well-articulated hands, carrying an unusual scorching heat, were slowly wandering along her slender, delicate waistline.

The roughness of the palms grazed her tender skin, causing it to quiver slightly.

A scorching, heavy body pressed down, fitting seamlessly, trapping her beneath him.

Hot, heavy breaths blew against the most sensitive patch of skin on her neck, raising a field of goosebumps.

She could feel that person's body temperature, tall and upright, his aura scorching and domineering, carrying an unfamiliar, dizzying aggressiveness.

She wanted to see him clearly.

Urgently, anxiously, she wanted to touch that face so close at hand.

Her vision was hazy, light and shadow swaying, catching only a glimpse of breathtaking allure, at the tail end of that person's eye, a demonic, dazzling red tear mole.

Vibrant as a drop of blood, yet resembling a brand.

"Mm..." A shattered sob escaped her throat, whether from pain or something else, she could not tell.

"Has the young miss woken up?" The maid Liuying kept her voice extremely low, terrified of disturbing the person inside the bed curtains from her sweet dream.

Layers upon layers of smoke-pink bed curtains were parted ever so slightly by a boneless, slender hand.

"Mn~"

A very soft whimper, wrapped in thick, unmelting sleepiness, drifted out from deep within the curtains.

The voice carried a touch of post-sleep huskiness, cloyingly sweet and softly captivating.

She seemed to have had a seductive dream, yet she could not remember a single thing.

Liuying couldn't help pressing her lips into a smile; hearing her young miss's waking sounds like this would melt anyone's heart into a pool of spring water.

"Young Miss, it's time to get up," Liuying coaxed softly again, carefully hooking up the bed curtains.

The scenery inside the bed was finally clear.

On the wide, luxurious carved-wood platform bed, a figure was half-reclining.

Wen Qionghua, the apple of the eye and the tip of the heart that the Xuanhe Prince's Estate had prayed for a full three generations to finally receive.

"What time is it?" Wen Qionghua spoke, every word like a honey-coated feather, gently scratching at one's heart.

"Replying to the Young Miss, it has just passed past nine in the morning," Liuying lowered her head.

Another round-faced maid named Bitao had already stepped forward carrying a bowl of warm rose-scented dew.

Wen Qionghua picked up the cup and took a few small sips, her pink tongue unconsciously licking her petal-full lips, leaving behind a seductive trace of moisture.

"So weary," Wen Qionghua complained softly, her voice sticky and laced with a hint of spoiled coyness.

"The Young Miss's complexion is much better today," Bitao smiled as she combed her hair.

Wen Qionghua gave a soft humpf: "I coughed half the night again last night, how am I better?" As she spoke, she covered her mouth and coughed lightly twice, her slender shoulders trembling slightly.

Liuying hurriedly fetched a fox-fur cloak and draped it over her shoulders: "Young Miss, the water for today's medicinal bath is already prepared. Soaking in it will make you feel more comfortable."

Wen Qionghua languidly leaned against the soft pillow, letting her tie the complex clothing ribbons.

She was exceedingly beautiful, her brows like distant mountains touched with ink, her eyes like autumn waters rippling, the bridge of her nose high yet not overly so, and her lips like painted vermilion. Without a speck of powder, she was already peerless in beauty.

"Young Miss..." Bitao hesitated, stopping mid-sentence.

Wen Qionghua lazily lifted her eyelids: "What is it? Did a cat bite your tongue?"

As Bitao picked up the jade comb, she casually and nonchalantly spoke in a low voice: "Just a moment ago, Xiao Zhu from the second gate came to pass along a message, saying... saying he saw Young Master Xie."

"Young Master Xie?" Wen Qionghua's eyelashes didn't even flutter, her voice lazy, seemingly indifferent to news about this fiancé of hers.

Bitao peeked at her expression and lowered her voice even further, carrying a trace of hard-to-detect indignation, "Yes, Young Master Xie... he, he rented a storefront for that noodle-selling Liu girl... Many people saw it..."

The last few words were so soft they almost vanished into the rising mist, yet like a stone thrown into a calm lake, they instantly shattered the warm, hazy atmosphere of the room.

"Clatter!"

Wen Qionghua's fingertips loosened, and the jade cup holding the scented dew slipped from her grasp, rolling a few times on the floor and spilling a few sparkling droplets of water.

The air froze instantly.

Liuying and Bitao were frightened into silence, not daring to breathe loudly.

Everyone in the Prince's Estate knew that although this young miss was frail, she was the absolute treasure held in the palm of everyone's hand in the entire Xuanhe Prince's Estate.

Old Prince Xuanhe, Wen Jing, the only non-royal prince since the founding of the Li Kingdom, possessed illustrious military achievements and held the highest position among ministers.

The male line of the Prince's Estate was shockingly flourishing; the Old Prince had three sons, and each of the three sons had given birth exclusively to boys. In such a massive estate, there hadn't been a single cry of a baby girl.

Watching his colleagues' granddaughters, delicate as jade dolls, softly and sweetly calling "Grandfather," the Old Prince would grow so envious his eyes practically turned green.

The mistress of the First Estate, Wen Qionghua's biological mother Xiao Yan, after successively giving birth to three sons as robust as little calves, had long since given up hope of having a daughter.

Who would have thought that at nearly forty years old, she would unexpectedly become pregnant!

Yet the pregnancy was arduous, and the birth was a brush with death; she fought with half her life just to deliver a baby girl as thin as a kitten.

Wen Qionghua was born amidst the yearning gazes of the entire estate.

Her cries were so weak they were barely audible, and congenital ailments left her tiny body agonizingly fragile, so much so that even sucking milk drained all her strength.

Yet her arrival instantly lit up the gloomy skies of the entire Xuanhe Prince's Estate.

Holding this weightless granddaughter who seemed as if she would shatter at a touch, the Old Grandfather wept tears of joy and immediately slammed the key to his private treasury into his eldest son's hands: "Use it! Use it to your heart's content! Whatever Qionghua wants, pluck the stars from the sky if she asks!"

She was the pampered daughter the estate had prayed generations for, the sole pearl in the palm of the Xuanhe Prince's lineage.

Her constitution was so weak that she had to soak day in and day out in meticulously blended medicinal soups; the precious herbs consumed in those baths were valuable enough to feed a battalion of elite soldiers.

Perhaps due to chronic frailty and lack of stamina, Wen Qionghua was shockingly lazy. If she could lie down, she would never sit; if she could close her eyes, she would never open them.

Yet beneath this languidness hid a startling, crystalline cleverness.

The Old Prince doted on her boundlessly, and her three older brothers held her in the palms of their hands, terrified she would fall, keeping her in their mouths for fear she would melt.

Wen Qionghua collected her thoughts. She should have been angry, but an eerie flash of red suddenly flickered across her mind.

She couldn't remember it. She couldn't remember it at all. Yet inexplicably, it settled her racing thoughts.

"Let's go take the medicinal bath first..." Wen Qionghua wrinkled her dainty nose, as if this daily mandatory routine were far more distressing than the news she had just heard.

Seeing this, the two maids hurriedly coaxed her: "Today's medicinal bath has the newly delivered rose dew added to it. It smells divine."

Wen Qionghua reluctantly nodded, supported carefully by her maids as she walked toward the bathing room.

The bathing room was filled with curling mist and a charming fragrance.

Liuying and Bitao began to strip away Wen Qionghua's outer robe and undergarments. The cloud-like silk slipped away, piling onto the warm jade floor, revealing her true form of ice-like skin and jade-like bones.

Her skin was so delicate it lacked a single flaw, appearing as if a breath would break it. Her shoulder and neck lines were smooth and graceful, flowing down to full, voluptuous curves, while her waist was slender enough to be spanned by a single grasp, outlining a breathtaking arc.

Her pitch-black hair fell like a waterfall, barely concealing spots of intimate spring scenery, adding an even more evocative charm of unspoken temptation.

"Young Miss is truly beautiful," Bitao couldn't help praising as she carefully supported her step into the wooden tub.

Wen Qionghua languidly leaned against the rim of the tub. The steaming hot water flushed her cheeks, adding a touch of enchanting vibrancy.

"Young Miss, is the water temperature suitable?" Bitao asked softly.

Submerged in the medicinal bath, amidst the rising steam, a faint pink hue bloomed across Wen Qionghua's porcelain-white skin.

She closed her eyes and murmured an "Mn," tiny water droplets clinging to her long eyelashes. Only then did she begin to digest the news she had just received.

"Xie Linfeng...

chapters.title: Go Taste That Liu Girl's Plain Noodle Soup
chapters.content:
"Xie Linfeng rented a storefront for that surnamed Liu woman?"

Wen Qionghua's voice drifted out from the steam of the medicinal bath.

Bitao lowered her head, not daring to look at her young miss's expression: "Yes... it's a two-story storefront, right in the busiest section of the East Market."

The bathing room fell silent for a moment, save for the sound of gently rippling water. Wen Qionghua slowly closed her eyes, her long eyelashes casting two shadows upon her porcelain skin.

"Young Miss..." Bitao called out with lingering anxiety.

"Understood." Wen Qionghua finally spoke. Her voice remained soft and sweet, yet it carried no hint of whether she was angry or pleased.

"Is the Young Miss not angry?" Bitao couldn't help asking.

Wen Qionghua chuckled lightly, though it carried a hint of nonchalance: "What is there to be angry about? It's just a storefront."

She paused. "Besides, Xie Gongzi and I are not yet married. What he does, what business is it of mine?"

Though she said this, her fingertips unconsciously tightened.

Wen Qionghua closed her eyes, yet her heart was not entirely without ripples.

Xie Linfeng.

To her, this name felt more like a distant and hazy symbol.

The legitimate second son of Prime Minister Xie, the head of civil officials in the Li Kingdom, born into a prestigious and strict family.

It was said that when he was young, a wandering master fortune-teller prophesied that he would face a great calamity before turning twenty, and could only resolve it by quietly practicing asceticism before the Buddha.

Therefore, this jade-like scion of the Xie family spent five years in quiet cultivation at Great Awakening Temple, a royal monastery in the suburbs of the capital. Not only did this dispel his doom, but it also branded an indelible aura of Buddhist detachment and cold aloofness upon him.

Upon his return to the capital, owing to his peerless appearance and aloof, cold temperament, countless noble ladies in the capital secretly lost their hearts to him.

Now serving in the Hanlin Academy, he was said to be diligent and meticulous in his official duties.

As for Wen Qionghua, the sickly weakling held in the palms of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate who rarely stepped beyond the inner courtyard, she was his destined fiancée.

This marriage alliance stemmed from an imperial decree written by the late emperor.

Back then, the Xuanhe Prince's Estate desperately yearned for a daughter in vain, leaving the betrothal like castles in the air. It wasn't until Wen Qionghua was born that this weighty engagement finally found its destination.

Even though Mr. and Mrs. Wen felt a thousand reluctance and unwillingness to hand such a precious treasure over to a man so cold he seemed devoid of mortal warmth, the late emperor's decree carried imperial words; how could they dare disobey?

Thus, this marriage became an accepted fact tacitly acknowledged throughout the capital.

Wen Qionghua herself held no great affection for Xie Linfeng. With her frail body and confinement within the estate year-round, she was inherently indifferent to matters of romance and lacked the energy to waste on them.

She only vaguely knew that she had a fiancé, who was the notoriously cold-tempered young master of the Xie family.

She had never even actively inquired about him. Her days had her own rhythm of living; with her family's unconditional doting, a pavilion full of treasures, and rare medicines nourishing her body, she felt nothing was lacking.

However, the existence of this engagement genuinely brought her trouble.

Xie Linfeng was the unreachable white moonlight of countless maidens in the capital, yet he fell into the hands of a sickly weakling who "gasp for breath every three steps" and was "ill-fated with short life."

Those overt and covert jealousies, taunts, pities, and even malicious speculations drifted through the high walls of the Prince's Estate like annoying willow catkins in spring, omnipresent.

Being of lazy temperament, she couldn't be bothered to care about these idle gossips, finding them merely noisy.

However, this did not mean she could tolerate others looking down on her, nor did she tolerate her future husband making a scandalous farce of "hiding a beauty in a golden house" before their marriage.

She didn't care about Xie Linfeng as a person, but she cared deeply about her future peace and quiet.

A fiancé who entangled himself with a noodle-selling woman before marriage and even set up businesses for her, in what kind of awkward and ridiculous position would that place her, Wen Qionghua?

She only wished to live her pampered, lazy days peacefully and quietly.

Xie Linfeng's actions undoubtedly added countless troubles to her already precarious health and lazy lifestyle.

"A hero saving a damsel in distress..."

Wen Qionghua repeated these four words in her heart once more, and that trace of extremely faint mockery surfaced at the corners of her lips again.

"Young Miss... please don't take it to heart," Liuying watched her expression carefully, weighing her words before speaking,

"Xie Gongzi... perhaps he saw that Liu girl was lonely and pitiful, and felt a moment of compassion? After all, he practiced asceticism in a temple; having a merciful heart is only natural..."

"A merciful heart?"

Wen Qionghua finally spoke again, her voice clear and cool: "The Xie family young master's merciful heart is truly quite valuable. A two-story storefront in the East Market... how many bowls of plain noodle soup does that Liu girl need to sell to earn it back?"

She said no more, letting Liuying and Bitao help her out of the wooden tub, wrapping her in a cloud-brocade soft towel and wiping her carefully.

Upon leaving the warm medicinal bath, her jade-like skin faintly flushed with a chilly undertone, making her appear even more fragile and easily broken.

Wen Qionghua stood before the bronze mirror. The maiden in the glass possessed skin like snow and features like a painting, beautiful beyond mortal realms.

Changing into soft, comfortable moon-white night robes and returning to the warm, fragrant sleeping chambers, Wen Qionghua lazily leaned against the daybed by the window.

The sunlight outside the window was pleasant, passing through the exquisite carved window lattice to cast mottled light and shadows upon her. She held a scroll of books in her hands, yet had not turned a single page for a long time.

Liuying and Bitao exchanged a glance, both seeing worry in each other's eyes.

Their young miss, though quiet at the moment, clearly hid a hard-to-detect trace of chill beneath that lazy aura that was even more intense than usual.

"Young Miss! Young Miss!" A crisp voice interrupted her train of thought.

A maid of twelve or thirteen rushed in frantically, crying, "The three young masters heard about Xie Gongzi's affair and were furious! They've already taken people and headed to the Xie Estate!"

The jade comb in Wen Qionghua's hand slipped to the floor with a "clack." She abruptly stood up, but a wave of dizziness washed over her due to the sudden movement, nearly causing her to fall. Liuying hurriedly steadied her: "Young Miss, don't rush, the Young Master and the others are just going to demand an explanation..."

"Nonsense!" Wen Qionghua raised her voice, a rare flush appearing on her pale face. "Quick, I must go stop them!"

When Wen Qionghua hurriedly rushed to the front courtyard, her three brothers were already dressed and adorned, their faces filled with rage. Eldest brother Wen Jing held a riding whip, second brother Wen Rui wore a sword at his waist, and third brother Wen Yu, though the youngest, also wore the stance of someone ready to fight to the death.

"What are my brothers doing?" Wen Qionghua blocked the doorway, her slender body shivering slightly in the cold wind.

"Jiaojia, stay out of this!"; this was Wen Qionghua's childhood name. Wen Jing raged, "That scoundrel Xie Linfeng dares to treat you with such disdain! We're going to give him a piece of our minds today!"

"Exactly!" Wen Rui echoed, "The apple of our Wen family's eye; how can we allow others to humiliate her like this?"

Wen Qionghua looked at her three furious brothers, feeling both touched and helpless.

She said softly, "Brothers, don't be hasty. There might be hidden reasons behind this. Let me go see Xie Gongzi first and ask him clearly."

"No!" The three brothers spoke in unison.

Wen Jing stepped forward: "Jiaojia, your health is weak. Leave these matters to your brothers to handle. If that Xie Linfeng really dares to fail you, I'll be the first to refuse!"

Wen Qionghua looked at her fiercely protective brothers and suddenly smiled. That smile was fleeting, breathtakingly gorgeous: "Rest assured, brothers, though Qionghua is sickly, she is not someone to be bullied at will. I have my own plans for this matter, so I ask my brothers to remain calm and collected."

She turned to Liuying and said, "Go prepare, I'm going out."

"Where is the Young Miss going?" Liuying asked in surprise.

A calm glint flashed in Wen Qionghua's eyes: "Naturally, to go taste that Liu girl's plain noodle soup."

chapters.title: A Bowl of Plain Noodle Soup
chapters.content:
The night was heavy. One by one, the lamps in the Imperial Academy were extinguished, save for the innermost study where a faint glow still lingered.

Xie Linfeng put down his brush and rubbed the bridge of his nose. His desk was piled high with documents awaiting his review; he had once again busied himself deep into the night.

"Lord Xie, would you care for some late-night refreshment?" a young attendant asked softly from outside the door.

Xie Linfeng shook his head, stood up, and draped an outer robe over his shoulders: "No need. I'm going out for a walk."

He had never favored the midnight snacks prepared by the cooks in his own estate, but instead grew quite fond of an inconspicuous noodle stall in the East Market. The stall keeper, an elderly man in his fifties with the surname Liu, ran this tiny patch of the world alongside his daughter, Sanniang.

The noodle stall was crude, a few wooden tables, a few low stools, and a dim, yellowish oil lamp suspended from the roof of the canopy, swaying gently in the night breeze. Every time Xie Linfeng came, he would invariably take the seat in the very corner and order a bowl of the most ordinary plain noodle soup; clear broth and watery noodles, yet it inexplicably suited his palate.

That day, no sooner had he seated himself than he heard a burst of arguing coming from behind the stall.

"Father! Eldest Brother and Second Brother are here to shake you down for money again!" Sanniang's voice carried a crying tone. "This is our last bit of silver! If we give it to them, we won't even be able to buy flour tomorrow!"

"Sanniang, they are, after all, your brothers..." The old man coughed, his voice weak.

"What kind of brothers are they! All day long they idle about, gambling and drinking, when have they ever cared whether we live or die?" Sanniang's voice trembled with rage. "If you give it to them today, I'm going to the authorities!"

"Smack!" A resounding slap echoed through the air.

"Vile wench! How dare you talk back to your brothers?" a crude male voice cursed. "Father, just look at this attitude of hers. How is she ever going to get married in the future?"

Xie Linfeng frowned slightly and raised his gaze.

Behind the stall stood two disheveled men with coarse, fleshy faces and fierce expressions, currently grabbing Sanniang by the collar. Sanniang was only seventeen or eighteen years old, delicate and pretty. At that moment, her cheek was red and swollen, and tears brimmed in her eyes, yet she stubbornly bit her lip, refusing to let herself cry out.

Xie Linfeng originally had no desire to meddle in other people's business, but the girl's eyes inexplicably reminded him of an injured bird he had seen in a temple during his youth; even though it was in immense pain, it still struggled and refused to lower its head.

He put down his chopsticks, stood up, and walked over.

"Might the gentlemen keep it down a bit?" His voice was clear and cold, yet brook no argument.

The two ruffians were startled and turned to appraise him. Seeing his luxurious attire and extraordinary bearing, they dared not act presumptuously for a moment.

"This young master, this is our family matter, no need to trouble yourself," one of them forced a smile.

Xie Linfeng swept a cool glance over him: "Since it is a family matter, it should not disturb others while they eat."

His tone was calm, yet inexplicably made people dare not retort. The two ruffians exchanged glances; after all, they dared not offend a person of high status, so they let go resentfully. Before leaving, they still glared viciously at Sanniang: "Vile wench, we'll settle accounts with you later!"

Sanniang kept her head down, her shoulders trembling slightly, yet she still stood there stubbornly.

Xie Linfeng glanced at her, said nothing, and turned back to his seat.

A moment later, a steaming bowl of plain noodle soup was brought over. Xie Linfeng looked down to find the noodle broth clear, the noodles fine and white, topped with a golden-yellow poached egg; the plain noodle soup he usually ordered never came with an egg.

He raised his eyes and met Sanniang's nervous gaze.

"Young master, just now... thank you." Her voice was very soft, the tips of her ears slightly red. "This egg... is a token of gratitude."

Xie Linfeng paused, but ultimately did not refuse, saying only indifferently: "A mere trifle."

He lowered his head to eat his noodles, and Sanniang quietly retreated, failing to notice the young woman's bounding joy after she turned away.

From then on, every time Xie Linfeng came to eat noodles, there would always be something extra in his bowl; sometimes an egg, sometimes a few rare slices of cured meat. Sanniang never spoke too much; she would only quietly watch him with those clear eyes, then quickly dart away.

This was the most inconspicuous yet most practical way of showing gratitude she could think of. She didn't know who he was, only hearing others call him "Lord Xie," only knowing he was a person of noble standing in the Imperial Academy, and even less did she know that he was already betrothed. She simply wanted to repay him purely, carrying a hint of a young maiden's budding romantic sentiment.

Xie Linfeng was not blind to a young maiden's feelings, but bearing a betrothal to the Prince of Xuanhe's estate, he could only pretend not to know. Until that day, when he found the noodle stall closed.

For three consecutive days, that familiar lantern failed to light up. Xie Linfeng felt a restless and inexplicable unease in his heart; thinking of those clear yet stubborn eyes, it felt as though something vital was missing.

Upon inquiring among the neighbors, he learned that Old Man Liu had suddenly fallen gravely ill and passed away. To make matters worse, the Liu family's two unfilial sons were planning to sell their younger sister to a widower in his fifties on the west side of the city in exchange for a bride price.

When Xie Linfeng found Sanniang, she was nearly being dragged away by force, clutching tightly in her hand the only silver hairpin her mother had left behind, her eyes filled with the determination to die. The young girl had lost a layer of weight, her eyes red and swollen like peaches, yet she stubbornly refused to shed a tear.

"Lord Xie..." Seeing him, she frantically hid the silver hairpin behind her back, "I, I was only..."

Xie Linfeng was silent for a moment, then suddenly said, "I can help you."

The young woman merely shook her head through her tears.

"There is a shopfront in the East Market up for rent. You are good at making noodles; I can buy the lease for you to run it."

Sanniang had wanted to refuse, but as an orphaned girl, she was already at her wit's end.

She bit her lip, holding back her tears: "Lord Xie's kindness, Sanniang will engrave it on her heart. But this shop, let it be considered a loan from you, Lord Xie! Sanniang will surely run it well, and once she earns money, she will repay you down to the very last coin! If she cannot pay it back... if she cannot pay it back, Sanniang is willing to serve you like an ox or a horse to repay the debt!"

Xie Linfeng looked at her stubborn appearance, was silent for a moment, and finally nodded.

He did indeed harbor a selfish motive: this noodle stall... was one of the few places where he could briefly catch his breath and feel a touch of human warmth. He did not wish to see it vanish. To this reason, he had never probed deeply himself, let alone acknowledge whether any other emotions had mingled within it.

Thus, Xie Linfeng helped Sanniang secure a two-courtyard shopfront in the East Market.

He had originally meant well, not knowing that the gossip in the capital had already spread like wildfire; that the young master of the Xie family had spent a thousand pieces of gold for the sake of a noodle-selling girl, even willing to offend the apple of the Prince of Xuanhe's eye.

"Lord Xie, have you heard?" That day, while Xie Linfeng was organizing case files in the Imperial Academy, a colleague sidled up to him with a mysterious air. "The carriage of the Prince of Xuanhe's estate went toward the East Market; rumor has it Miss Wen went herself..."

The brush in Xie Linfeng's hand paused, the ink blooming into a smudge across the paper. Wen Qionghua? That sickly weakling rumored to be frail beyond measure; why would she suddenly go to the East Market?

A terrifying thought flashed through his mind, could she be going to make trouble for Sanniang? Xie Linfeng's heart abruptly plummeted! An ominous prehension seized him instantly. Wen Qionghua! How could she go there?! What was she planning to do to Sanniang?!

At this thought, Xie Linfeng could no longer sit still. He hastily requested leave, vaulted onto his horse, and galloped furiously toward the East Market. Xie Linfeng was ordinarily cold and self-restrained, but at this moment he felt a rush of hot blood surge straight to his head. The cold wind lashed at his face like a knife, yet he only begrudged his horse for not running fast enough.

chapters.title: People of No Consequence
chapters.content:
On the bustling streets of the East Market, an extremely opulent carriage slowly came to a halt.

A foot clad in cloud-brocade soft satin embroidered shoes stepped lightly onto the footstool. Immediately following, a slender and delicate figure was supported down from the carriage by two maidservants, one on each side, almost in a half-embraced, half-carried manner.

In an instant, it seemed as though even the turbid air in the alley was instantly purified.

Wen Qionghua was dressed in an utterly plain moon-white gown, draped with a silver-fox fur cloak, which made her porcelain-white skin appear almost transparent.

Her raven-black, waterfall-like hair was loosely gathered with a simple jade hairpin, a few stray locks hanging by her cheeks, adding an extra touch of languid, sickly beauty. Her brows were like distant mountains touched with dark pigment, her eyes like autumn waters rippling, and her lips were extremely pale, resembling newly bloomed cherry blossoms. Her entire person was as exquisite and fragile as a glazed beauty, as if a gust of wind could blow her away.

The moment she appeared, the entire street fell silent for a fraction of a moment.

"Is that... Miss Wen of the Prince of Xuanhe's estate?" someone whispered in astonishment.

"Heavens, she actually came in person!"

"Could she be here to cause trouble for Sanniang?"

Wen Qionghua remained completely indifferent to the surrounding discussion. She merely cast a cool glance at the shopfronts along the street and asked softly, "The Liu family noodle shop, where is it?"

Liuying lowered her voice: "Miss, it's right around the corner ahead."

Wen Qionghua nodded and walked slowly in that direction.

She walked extremely slowly, as if every step consumed a great deal of effort, yet her spine was held straight as a ramrod, like a proud plum blossom defying the snow, aloof and solitary.

At the street corner, Sanniang was lowering her head to knead dough when she suddenly felt the surrounding area grow quiet. She looked up in puzzlement and met Wen Qionghua's clear, limpid eyes.

"You..." Sanniang froze.

Wen Qionghua looked at her quietly, the corners of her lips curving slightly: "Girl, do you still have plain noodle soup?"

Wen Qionghua appraised the young maiden before her. Sanniang was delicate and pretty; though wearing coarse cloth garments, she was neatly and cleanly put together. At this moment, her eyes were filled with panic, yet she stubbornly straightened her back, refusing to show cowardice.

"I heard the plain noodle soup here is quite good," Wen Qionghua spoke, her voice as melodious as a clear spring. "Bring me a bowl."

Sanniang was stunned, clearly not expecting this high-born noble lady to actually be here to eat noodles. Snapping out of her daze from the other's beauty, she hurriedly invited Wen Qionghua to sit at the cleanest table in the shop, using her sleeve to wipe down an already gleaming tabletop once more.

"Please wait a moment, Miss. The noodles will be ready right away," Sanniang said, then turned and went into the kitchen.

Wen Qionghua glanced around. The shop was not large, but it was kept in good order. A few simple paintings and calligraphy scrolls hung on the walls, and fresh wildflowers sat on the tables, revealing attentive care everywhere.

Just as Wen Qionghua was lost in thought, the shop door was suddenly flung open with a crash. A tall figure swept in amidst the cold wind; it was Xie Linfeng, who had hurried over in a rush.

His moon-white robe was slightly disheveled from his frantic ride, and a few stray locks of hair on his forehead were dampened with sweat, yet it did not detract in the least from his aloof and cold demeanor.

The moment his ink-dark, profound eyes locked onto Wen Qionghua, a trace of complex emotion flashed through them. Wen Qionghua raised her eyes, her gaze locking with her betrothed's across the space. This was their first time meeting in an unofficial setting, yet under such a delicate and subtle context.

At that moment, Sanniang emerged from the kitchen. Hoping to ask the esteemed guest if she had any dietary restrictions, she instead caught sight of two people who looked as though they had stepped out of a painting, staring fixedly at each other.

An inexplicable sourness surged into her heart; she had a fair idea of who this woman might be. She turned to leave, but was grabbed by Xie Linfeng, who pulled her behind him to shield her.

Xie Linfeng wore a frigid expression, his tone laced with warning: "Miss Wen, if you have any grievances, direct them at me, Xie. What's the point of making things difficult for a young girl?"

Wen Qionghua was stunned for a split second, then laughed out of sheer anger. Ignoring the man before her entirely, she asked Liuying and Bitao, "Did I make things difficult for her?"

Liuying and Bitao were already incensed, clenching their fists and grinding their teeth as they said, "Naturally not! Our miss came here simply to have a bowl of noodle soup."

She then asked the person standing behind him, "Did I make things difficult for you?"

Sanniang was still dazed at this point, but she answered truthfully nonetheless: "The young lady merely asked me for a bowl of plain noodle soup."

Xie Linfeng's complexion gradually paled, revealing a rare trace of awkwardness.

"Young master, what are you doing?" Sanniang cautiously tugged at Xie Linfeng's sleeve, then, feeling it was inappropriate, hurriedly turned and retreated back into the kitchen.

The air in the shop seemed to freeze. Xie Linfeng's gaze darted back and forth between Wen Qionghua and the direction of the kitchen, seemingly trying to deduce the purpose of her visit.

Meanwhile, Wen Qionghua sat composed and leisurely, her slender fingers tapping gently against the table, producing a faint, rhythmic sound, completely ignoring the man who stood rooted like a wooden stake.

Right at that moment, Sanniang emerged carrying a steaming bowl of plain noodle soup topped with chopped scallions, walking over with cautious steps.

Keeping her head down and avoiding Xie Linfeng's gaze, she gently placed the noodle bowl onto the table, which was covered with a piece of white silk, in front of Wen Qionghua, her voice as thin as a mosquito's hum: "Esteemed guest... your noodles are ready."

Wen Qionghua's gaze fell upon the bowl of noodles: clear broth, white noodles, a few flecks of emerald-green scallions.

She picked up a pair of bamboo chopsticks, which had likewise been polished to a brilliant shine, moving with the grace of plucking a flower. She lifted a few strands of noodles, blew on them gently, and brought them to her petal-pink lips.

Everyone's gaze was focused on her, including Xie Linfeng's.

Wen Qionghua chewed slowly and deliberately, her movements exceedingly unhurried. After a long moment, she put down her chopsticks, picked up a silk handkerchief, gently pressed the corners of her mouth, and raised her eyes to look at Sanniang, whose fingers were practically wringing her apron to pieces out of tension.

Just when Xie Linfeng expected her to utter some caustic or nitpicking remark, he heard her speak in a soft, completely flat tone:

"Mm. The broth is clear and flavorful, and the noodles are chewy."

She paused, her gaze seemingly sweeping casually across Sanniang's face. The faint arc of her lips seemed to deepen by a fraction, her voice remaining soft and light:

"Good craftsmanship."

With that, she looked at no one else, merely furrowed her brow slightly, covered her mouth, and coughed twice more, her voice carrying a trace of fatigue: "Liuying, Bitao, let's return to the estate. I'm tired."

Liuying and Bitao immediately stepped forward to carefully support her.

Amidst the attendance of her maids, Wen Qionghua walked out of the noodle shop with graceful poise. From beginning to end, she did not spare Xie Linfeng another glance, as though he were merely a passerby of no consequence.

"Oh, and by the way, I heard the Xie estate still has an eldest young master?" Wen Qionghua suddenly turned back as she lifted the fabric curtain. Without waiting for Xie Linfeng's reply, she curved her lips into a smile and departed.

Xie Linfeng stood rooted to the spot, watching that slender, delicate figure vanish into the luxurious carriage, listening to the rumbling sound of the wheels crushing against the bluestone pavement gradually fade away. He lowered his head to look at the stool where Wen Qionghua had sat, draped in snowy white silk, but now empty.

Xie Linfeng only felt a rush of anger blocked in his chest, neither rising nor falling. All the cross-examinations he had prepared appeared so laughable and redundant in the face of her utterly innocent yet seemingly all-knowing attitude. An unprecedented wave of irritability and... an indescribable sense of defeat washed over him like a tide of icy water, instantly engulfing him.

chapters.title: Utterly Boring
chapters.content:
Wen Qionghua returned to Qionghua Pavilion, leaning against the soft couch by the window. Watching the begonia petals falling softly outside, her expression remained calm and detached.

Liuying and Bitao exchanged a cautious glance, carefully helping her change into soft slippers and bringing in hot tea and dim sum. Qionghua, however, merely gave a slight shake of her head, signaling them to withdraw.

Though the carriage had driven away from the bustling alleyways of the East Market, it could not wash away the chill in her heart.

The way Xie Linfeng had rushed into the noodle shop looking like he was facing a formidable enemy, eager to play the knight in shining armor, was like a cold needle piercing her habitually lazy and indifferent mood.

"Hah..." She let out a very faint, derisive scoff, heavy with deep fatigue.

Did he actually think she had gone there to give someone a hard time?

Qionghua lazily rolled over, her fingertips lightly toying with the jade hairpin on the table, thinking to herself: "This Xie Linfeng, if he's truly self-righteous, he's also truly a fool."

If she, Wen Qionghua, had truly wanted to make things difficult for Sanniang, why would she need to go in person? A single glance from her would be enough for others to handle the matter cleanly.

Yet, she disdained to do so.

She disdained bullying an innocent woman, and even more, she disdained fighting for affection with a noodle-selling girl.

"My lady, have a sip of ginseng soup to warm yourself up," Liuying said, holding a cup of warm ginseng soup and carefully urging, "A filthy place like that; it only dirtied your eyes. It's not worth getting angry over."

Qionghua didn't take it; she merely rolled over lazily, burying her face a little deeper. Angry? Not really. It was more of... boredom, utter and absolute boredom.

She saw things too clearly. Xie Linfeng's actions today had nailed his entanglement with Sanniang out in the open.

Even if the Xie family, constrained by social standing, would never allow a noodle-selling girl to cross their threshold, let alone become Xie Linfeng's legitimate wife, so what? Sanniang's existence would be like a thorn, forever wedged between her and Xie Linfeng.

She was the sole legitimate granddaughter of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate across three generations, a precious treasure forged of wealth and status. If she married into the Xie family, she would represent the reputation of both the Wen and Xie families, the proper decorum decreed by an imperial edict.

She had to be dignified, magnanimous, and play the role of the perfect mistress of the household. She could not display jealousy or lose her composure. Because she was a "young lady of a prestigious house," she was born to bear the shackles brought by this "decorum."

And what about Sanniang? An orphaned girl drifting through life, stubbornly fighting for survival, in Xie Linfeng's heart, and in the eyes of onlookers ignorant of the truth, she would forever be the "pitiable," "innocent," and "sympathetic" one.

In the decades to come, every single thing Wen Qionghua did or said in the Xie family might be compared to that lingering "white moonlight." No matter how well she did, it would be taken for granted; the slightest misstep would be branded as bullying the weak and abusing power.

If Xie Linfeng could glare at her today for Sanniang's sake without asking about right and wrong, what about the future? In his eyes, Wen Qionghua would always be the " villain" who might "make things difficult" for his beloved.

"Matching eyebrows in mutual respect? Treating each other like honored guests?" Qionghua mocked silently in her heart. "I'm afraid even the surface pretense won't be maintained."

All she asked for was a quiet sanctuary of her own, a place where she could lazily and comfortably nurse this frail body of hers. Yet this betrothal was destined to drag her into an endless vortex of suspicion, guardedness, and gossip.

She wasn't afraid of fighting; she just felt... tired. Expending so much mental energy to contend and fight over a man she didn't care about at all, and a woman who was equally innocent yet destined to become a sacrifice; it was simply too boring.

Amidst her vexation, a rush of hurried and chaotic footsteps came from outside, accompanied by muffled sobs and anxious whispers. Immediately afterward, her mother, Madam Xiao, and her two aunts hurried in.

"Jiaojiao! My child!" The voice arrived before the person. Xiao Yanhong, the Princess of Xuanhe, had red-rimmed eyes and practically lunged into Qionghua Pavilion, followed by Madam Li of the second branch and Madam Wang of the third branch, both looking equally worried.

"Mother, Aunts..." Qionghua was just about to prop herself up when her mother pushed her right back onto the couch.

"Lie down! Just lie down!" Madam Xiao looked her daughter up and down, and seeing that her complexion was even paler than when she went out, her heart ached so much that tears fell in patters.

"You child! How... how could you run off to a place like that? A filthy place like that; what if it brought bad luck? Do you still want your health or not? Was it worth dragging yourself through the mud for that bastard?" Clearly, she had already heard everything that happened at the East Market noodle shop.

Madam Li, the second aunt, also chimed in anxiously, "Exactly! Qionghua, you are the apple of our entire household's eye! For that Xie boy to act like this, he clearly has no regard for our Wen family! Your father and your brothers have already gone to the Xie family to demand an explanation!"

Madam Wang, the third aunt, had an even more impatient temperament and said bitterly, "What a noble and refined young master! In my eyes, he's just an ungrateful fool bewitched by some common vixen! Jiaojiao, don't be afraid. With your aunts here, we will certainly not let you suffer such a grievance! That cheap maid Liu; I'll have someone go right now and..."

"Third Aunt!" Qionghua spoke up suddenly, her voice not loud, but carrying an unquestionable coolness. She raised her eyes, her calm gaze sweeping across her three closest relatives. "This matter has nothing to do with Sanniang."

All three matrons were stunned.

"Nothing to do with her?" Xiao Yanhong wiped her tears. "If she hadn't seduced..."

"Mother," Qionghua interrupted her mother, her tone carrying a weary firmness. "She is an orphan, merely trying to find a way to survive. If Xie Linfeng wanted to help her, or... harbored other thoughts, that is Xie Linfeng's affair. The fault does not lie with her."

Qionghua saw it clearly. Sanniang's gaze was clean and stubborn, devoid of any calculated clinging. She was merely unfortunate enough to become the vessel for Xie Linfeng's bit of "compassion" or "alternative affection," and even more unfortunately, she had been dragged into the muddy waters of her, Wen Qionghua.

"Then... then are we just going to let it go like this?" Third Aunt Wang was unwilling to accept it.

"Even if we don't let it go, what can we do?" Qionghua retorted, her voice drifting and light. "Have Father and Brothers storm into the Xie family? Force the Xie family to deal with Sanniang? Or make Xie Linfeng take a public oath? Would that be useful?"

She paused, looking at her mother and aunts who were rendered speechless by her words. Though she couldn't bear to, she continued, "When the heart is not there, a forced melon is not sweet. Suppressing one Sanniang today might bring a Li Sanniang or a Zhang Sanniang tomorrow. If Xie Linfeng truly had a shred of a place for me in his heart, he wouldn't have treated me that way today. Since he has no heart, why should I force it? This betrothal was decreed by the late emperor in the first place; it binds the Wen and Xie families, not me and Xie Linfeng as individuals."

Listening to her daughter's clear-headed, coldly rational analysis, Madam Xiao felt as though her heart had been carved out, and she wept uncontrollably, "My wretched child... your father and I are useless... If only we could have called off this betrothal back then..."

"Mother, it cannot be called off." Qionghua grasped her mother's hand. Her hand was ice-cold, yet it carried a comforting strength. "An imperial decree from the late emperor, his words carry the weight of gold. The Wen and Xie families, one civil and one military, are tied to the imperial court. This betrothal is about face, but even more, it is about responsibility."

She took a deep breath, as if making up her mind, and her gaze swept across her mother and two aunts as she slowly said, "However, the betrothal merely states that the Wen and Xie families shall be joined in marriage, it does not... specify by name that I, Wen Qionghua, must marry Xie Linfeng."

"Does the Xie family not have another eldest son?"

chapters.title: Swapping the Marriage
chapters.content:
As soon as these words fell, Qionghua Pavilion instantly plunged into a dead silence.

All three matrons widened their eyes, staring in disbelief at the pale, frail young girl on the couch who looked as though a gust of wind could blow her over.

"Jia-Jiaojiao... you... what do you mean by this?" Madam Xiao's voice was trembling.

Qionghua sat up straight. Though still wrapped in a thick plush blanket, her spine was held straight, and her gaze was clear and sharp. "I mean that the Xie family does not have only one eligible young master."

"You mean... that... eldest concubine-born son of the Xie family?" Second Aunt Li gasped, her expression changing completely.

Madam Lin's expression shifted slightly as she lowered her voice and said, "Jiaojiao, do you... do you know who that Xie Linyuan is?"

Qionghua tilted her head slightly, wearing a half-smile. "I know. A dissolute rake, right?"

Xie Linyuan, the eldest concubine-born son of the Xie family.

Xie Linyuan's background was an open secret among the noble houses of the capital.

Back then, Lord Xie, Xie Changlin, was not yet the Chancellor, but served as the Junior Minister of the Court of State Ceremonies. It was a time of border turmoil, and he was ordered to the border for peace negotiations, staying there for over a year. When he returned, he was actually carrying an infant boy still in swaddling clothes, claiming the child was born to a woman at the border. The woman had died in difficult childbirth, leaving him no choice but to bring the child back.

The elderly patriarch of the Xie family flew into a rage, immediately fetching the family rules and beating his son until he couldn't get out of bed for half a month. But since the child had already been brought back, they couldn't just throw him out, so they had no choice but to acknowledge him.

Later, Chancellor Xie married a wife of matching social standing, the legitimate daughter of the Minister of Revenue, and she gave birth to Xie Linfeng, thus producing a legitimate son.

Having a concubine-born son before a legitimate one was a major taboo in prestigious households, and to make matters worse, this eldest concubine-born son's biological mother had a mysterious background without even a proper title.

This eldest concubine-born son, Xie Linyuan, became the most awkward existence in the Xie family. Fortunately, Lord Xie still favored him quite a bit; it was said he treated him even better than Xie Linfeng. Otherwise, one could easily imagine what his life would have been like.

"So what if his biological mother is unknown?" Qionghua said lightly. "I am marrying a young master of the Xie family, not his birth mother."

Having a humble background and an unknown mother was one thing.

Yet he also happened to be a good-for-nothing rake!

All day long he indulged in cockfighting, dog-racing, and frequented pleasure houses; everyone in the capital knew he was a vagabond.

Madam Xiao shook her head anxiously. "Jiaojiao, how could that Xie Linyuan be worthy of you? You are the pearl held in the palm of our Wen family's hand. How can you..."

Qionghua had already anticipated the reactions of her mother and aunts. Her expression remained calm, even tinged with a hint of lazy fatigue. "Mother, don't rush. Hear me out."

"Mother, in your opinion... Is it better to marry a noble-minded gentleman whose heart is set on someone else, or a carefree rake?"

Madam Xiao was taken aback.

Qionghua lazily leaned back against the soft pillow, speaking leisurely:

"Xie Linfeng has Sanniang in his heart. For decades to come, no matter what I do, I will never surpass her."

"As for Xie Linyuan... he doesn't even have a heart."

"Since he has no heart, there won't be any 'white moonlight'."

"If I marry him, at least... I won't be wronged."

Wen's mother looked at her daughter's calm face, suddenly realizing something, and said tremulously, "Qionghua... could you be... could it be because of Xie Linfeng..."

"No." Qionghua interrupted her mother, her voice soft yet resolute. "Your daughter holds no affection for Xie Linfeng; I simply refuse to be a stumbling block in someone else's marriage, nor do I wish to live in the shadow of another person for the next few decades."

"That Xie Linyuan, the Chancellor's eldest concubine-born son, with an unknown mother and a lowly birth. That is his first flaw," she said steadily, as if stating a fact that had nothing to do with her. "Secondly, and most importantly, this man... is a notoriously dissolute playboy in the capital, indulging in cockfighting and dog-racing, accomplished in neither letters nor martial arts, an indelible stain on the Xie family."

"Then why do you still bring him up?!" Madam Xiao was so angry her whole body trembled.

"Precisely because he is such a 'stain'," Qionghua's gaze was unfathomably deep, "he is my best choice."

"Mother, think about it." She softened her tone, carrying a hint of coaxing yet helpless analysis. "If I marry Xie Linfeng, he is the legitimate second son upon whom the Xie family pins all their hopes, a refined and talented gentleman with a boundless future. I would bear the reputation of being 'jealous' and 'intolerant,' while constantly having to guard against that white moonlight in his heart. Everyone in the Xie family, including Xie Linfeng himself, would feel that I married above myself, keeping me constrained at every turn. How could I live such a life?"

"But what if I marry Xie Linyuan?" The corners of Qionghua's lips curved into a very faint, almost self-deprecating arc. "He is the concubine-born son the Xie family wishes they could hide away, a good-for-nothing despised by all. For me, the legitimate daughter of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate, to marry downward to him is a supreme 'favor' bestowed upon the Xie family! Everyone in the Xie family, including the Chancellor himself, must lower themselves by three notches in front of me! Because it is I, Wen Qionghua, who has condescended in a grievance to marry downward, lowering my noble status to 'harbor' this scourge for their Xie family!"

"As for Xie Linyuan himself..." A trace of indifference flashed across Qionghua's eyes. "Your daughter has heard that although he is profligate, he has never committed any truly heinous acts. Why should I care? Let him be as profligate as he pleases, as long as he stays out of my sight and doesn't bring those messy people into my presence. When I am in the Xie family, behind closed doors, I will still be the pampered young lady of the Prince's Estate; no one will dare to control me, no one will dare to question me. Won't the peace and quiet I desire finally be mine?"

The room fell into silence once more.

The third and second aunts looked at each other, momentarily unable to find any words of rebuttal.

Wen Qionghua paused, a flicker of resolute determination flashing in her eyes. "No matter how unworthy Xie Linyuan is, he can at least grant your daughter peace and quiet."

The room sank into a prolonged silence. Looking at her daughter's pale yet resolute face, Madam Xiao finally let out a long sigh: "If your decision is made... Mother... Mother will go and speak with your father."

Second Aunt blurted out anxiously, "Elder Sister-in-law! This..."

Madam Xiao raised a hand to halt her words. "Qionghua makes sense. Rather than marrying someone whose heart lies elsewhere, it is better to marry someone heartless. At least... at least my child won't have to suffer those grievances."

Seeing her mother holding back tears, Qionghua felt a pang in her heart. She knew this decision would subject her parents to much criticism in the imperial court, but compared to the unbearable indignities she might face after marrying Xie Linfeng, this was already the best choice.

"Mother need not worry," Qionghua said softly. "Your daughter knows what she is doing."

Madam Xiao stroked her daughter's cheek and choked out, "My child is so sensible it breaks my heart..."

After a moment of hesitation, Third Aunt asked doubtfully, "But... will the Xie family agree?"

Qionghua chuckled softly, a flash of certainty gleaming in her eyes.

"They... will have no choice but to agree."

chapters.title: A Spendthrift?
chapters.content:
At the same time, the Xie Residence.

The atmosphere was as oppressive as the calm before a storm. Prime Minister Xie Changlin sat at the head of the study with a dark expression, while Xie Linfeng stood below, his face equally livid.

Prince Xuanhe, Wen Jing, and the Heir Apparent, Wen Jing, had just flicked their sleeves and left, the rebukes and anger they left behind threatening to blow the roof off.

"Unfilial son!" Xie Changlin slammed his hand down on the desk, rattling the tea sets. "Look at the fine mess you've made! For a street-side noodle vendor, you actually publicly embarrassed the Wen family's young miss! Do you feel our Xie family hasn't lost enough face?!"

Xie Linfeng tightly pressed his lips together, his jawline taut. A trace of pale embarrassment still lingered on his face, but his eyes remained stubborn. "Father, today's matter was my rashness, and I misunderstood Miss Wen. But Miss Liu and I are completely innocent and aboveboard, with no illicit relations! For the Wen family to be so aggressive, how could they..."

"Silence!" Xie Changlin interrupted sternly. "Innocent and aboveboard? Then why did you buy a storefront for her? Why were you in such an impatient rush to rush over and protect her the moment you heard Miss Wen went to the noodle shop? Do you think everyone in the capital is blind?! Where do you expect Miss Wen to save face? Where do you expect the Xuanhe Prince's Estate to save face?!"

"Son... son only saw that she was alone and helpless..." Xie Linfeng tried to defend himself.

"There are plenty of people who are alone and helpless! How come I never see you helping anyone else?!" Xie Changlin was so angry his beard was trembling. "Aren't your duties in the Hanlin Academy enough to keep you busy? You just had to go looking for this trouble! Do you know that because of your actions today, the Wen family has already let word out that they are reconsidering this marriage!"

Xie Linfeng shuddered all over and suddenly looked up, the usual aloof self-control completely gone. "Reconsidering? They wouldn't dare! This was an imperial decree from the late emperor!"

"So what if it was an imperial decree from the late emperor?" Xie Changlin sneered. "The Wen family's prized treasure suffered a tremendous grievance at your place today, and Wen Jing, who always protects his own, is just supposed to swallow this anger? If he risks everything to make a scene before the Emperor and demands to call off the marriage even if it means punishment, do you really think His Majesty would risk his life tangling with the heavily guarded Prince Xuanhe just for the sake of 'reason'?!"

Xie Linfeng's face turned instantly white. He had never imagined the consequences could be so severe.

"Father, then... then what do we do now?" His voice carried a trace of imperceptible panic.

Xie Changlin wearily rubbed his glabella. "What else can we do? Prepare generous gifts, pick a day this week, and go personally to the Xuanhe Prince's Estate to apologize! Your attitude must be sincere, and your posture must be lowered! No matter what, stabilize the Wen family first! This marriage must not be lost!"

Just at that moment, the study door was pushed open with a loud, incredibly rude crash.

A heavy reeking of alcohol mixed with the cloying scent of cheap powder instantly filled the air.

A tall, disheveled young man was seen leaning lazily against the doorframe.

He wore a crimson brocade robe embroidered with gold thread, but the collar hung open and wrinkled, exposing a small expanse of solid chest.

His long hair was loosely tied with a gold ribbon, a few strands of stray hair sticking messily to his sweat-dampened temples. Yet this could not conceal a face so devastatingly beautiful it was almost bewitching; his narrow phoenix eyes slightly upturned, a black tear mole at the tail of his reddish-tinted eyes, making him look even more handsomely demonic.

The corners of his mouth, however, held an unconcerned, dissolute smile, and in his hand, he dragged an almost empty wine pot.

"Yo... Father, Second Brother... you're both here?" He spoke lazily, his voice carrying the hoarseness of a hangover and a careless levity. "I heard you arguing from far away... What's this? Is the sky falling?"

The newcomer was none other than the Xie family's eldest son by a concubine, whose birth mother was unknown and who was good for nothing, Xie Linyuan.

Seeing him in this state, Xie Changlin felt his anger flare up, but unable to bring himself to hit him, he could only rage, "Look at you, you ghost-like wretch! Where have you been carousing again?! Get out of my sight!"

Xie Linyuan acted as if he hadn't heard his father's roar. His gaze swept lazily past the scowling Xie Linfeng and landed back on Xie Changlin, letting out a scoff. "Carousing? Father, what are you saying... Your son merely went to the 'Drunken Immortal Tower' to listen to a few tunes and drink a few cups of flower wine. How could I compare to Second Brother... Tsk tsk, hiding a beauty in a golden house, scattering thousands of gold pieces on a storefront just to win a smile from the beauty; such a romantic affair has spread all over the capital! I heard... he even made the future younger sister-in-law angry?" Swaying as he walked to the desk, he unceremoniously picked up Xie Changlin's half-cup of cold tea and downed it in one gulp, the tea streaming down his chin onto his open collar.

"You...!" Xie Linfeng was so provoked by Xie Linyuan's frivolous words and actions that his face turned red with anger, his fists tightly clenched.

"What about me?" Xie Linyuan put down the tea cup, let out a loud burp, his eyes hazy yet carrying a trace of malicious amusement. "Second Brother, it's not that your older brother is lecturing you, but leaving such a celestial fiancée at home and running off to provoke some noodle-selling beauty? This taste... tsk tsk tsk..." He shook his head with an expression of heartbroken pity. "No wonder Miss Wen looks down on you and wants to call off the marriage!"

"Xie Linyuan!" Shaking with rage, Xie Linfeng grabbed the inkstone from the desk, preparing to hurl it.

Yet Xie Linyuan moved with a feigned clumsiness, swaying his steps just enough to dodge it entirely, while shouting, "Ayo! Father, look at him..." feigning grievance as if he had suffered a terrible wrong.

He wobbled over to stand right in front of Xie Linfeng, blowing breath thick with alcohol right into Xie Linfeng's face, lowering his voice with a malicious, bewitching tone. "Second brother... Tell me, if the Wen family really doesn't want you anymore... then your older brother... will I have the chance... to share our Xie family's... worries and solve our troubles? Hmm?" A flash of imperceptible shrewdness quickly flitted across those drunken phoenix eyes.

"You unfilial wretch! Get out! Get out of here immediately!" Xie Changlin's roar nearly blew the roof off.

Xie Linyuan laughed heartily, waving his hand carelessly as he picked up his empty wine pot. Staggering, humming an out-of-tune little ditty, he swayed out of the study, leaving behind a scene of utter wreckage and raging fury.

Watching his elder brother's debauched silhouette disappear out the door, and then thinking of Wen Qionghua's cool, calm eyes that seemed to see through everything, an unprecedented chill, mixed with a profound sense of the absurd and a latent unease, quietly crept up Xie Linfeng's spine.

He had a faint feeling that something was hurtling away in a completely out-of-control direction.

And that concubine-born elder brother whom he had always regarded as worthless trash and never once taken seriously was like a ghost lurking in the dark, grinning wide to reveal a sinister smile.

chapters.title: The Second Identity
chapters.content:
The atmosphere within the Xuanhe Prince's Estate had been exceptionally heavy these past few days.

The matter of the canceled marriage remained unresolved, and his daughter's wedding business felt like a poisonous thorn piercing deeply into Princess Xuanhe Consort Xiao's heart.

She fretted day and night, terrified that her daughter would harbor resentment in her heart and damage a constitution that was already frail to begin with.

Seeing that Qionghua, though still as listless and calm-looking as ever, had an inescapable weariness lingering between her brows, Consort Xiao's heart felt as though it were being twisted by a knife.

"Jiaojia, Mother thinks your energy has grown sparser lately, and you've been coughing more persistently at night."

Consort Xiao sat by Qionghua's couch, holding her daughter's icy hand with deep worry. "There are too many people and complicated matters in this estate, disturbing your peace. Why not... go stay at Dazhao Temple for a few days? Master Huiming is well-versed in medical principles, and the temple's environment is secluded, making it the best place for recuperation. It'll also just happen to be... a chance to calm your heart and pray before the Buddha."

Praying for blessings was false; wanting to distance her daughter from the capital's gossip and change the environment to relax her mind was the truth.

How could Qionghua not know her mother's intentions? She originally felt too lazy to go out, but looking at her mother's swollen eye rims and the deep worry pooled in the depths of her eyes, the refusal died on her lips.

Very well. Going out for a change of scenery would always do some good.

"Alright," Qionghua gently agreed. "I'll listen to Mother."

Consort Xiao was overjoyed and immediately set about making arrangements.

Early the next morning, a carriage that could hardly conceal its nobility carried Qionghua, along with Liuying and Bitao, quietly driving out of the capital under the covert escort of the estate's elite guards, heading toward Dazhao Temple on Yuntai Mountain in the northern suburbs.

Dazhao Temple sat halfway up Yuntai Mountain, surrounded by ancient trees reaching to the skies and the melodious chiming of bells and stone chimes.

Master Huiming personally settled Qionghua in "Tingsong Residence" (Pine-Listening Abode), the most secluded independent Zen courtyard on the back mountain.

This place was far from the clamor of the pilgrims in the front hall; pushing open the window revealed lush bamboo groves and babbling mountain streams, the air crisp and refreshing.

Qionghua did indeed feel somewhat relieved and refreshed.

During the day, she listened to sutras, read casual books, had Master Huiming take her pulse to adjust her medicine prescription, and slowly strolled in the courtyard supported by Liuying and Bitao.

Amidst the chirping of mountain birds, even her cough seemed to grow slightly lighter.

That night, Qionghua took the newly formulated herbal decoction.

The medicinal properties were somewhat fierce, churning in her stomach and banishing all sleepiness, leaving her instead somewhat restless and feverish.

Outside the window, the moonlight was just right. Listening to the rustle of bamboo leaves outside, she suddenly felt a stir of interest.

"Liuying, Bitao, you two go rest. I'll just sit here in the courtyard corridor for a bit of fresh air; you don't need to follow." Qionghua draped a plain cloak over her shoulders and instructed softly.

Seeing that her complexion was decent and her spirit was better than it had been during the day, and considering they were in this heavily guarded Zen courtyard, the two maids complied and withdrew, waiting only in the adjoining side room.

Qionghua walked out of the room alone.

The night was cool as water, carrying the unique botanical freshness of the mountain forest, making her stifled chest much more comfortable.

Before she knew it, she had walked to the side of the Zen courtyard near the back mountain's bamboo grove.

Here it was even more secluded, with only the rustling sound of wind blowing through bamboo leaves.

Suddenly!

A sound of air being split, extremely faint yet swift as the wind, interspersed with a few deeply suppressed groans and the crisp sound of weapon clashing, faintly drifted from the depths of the bamboo grove!

Qionghua's footsteps came to an abrupt halt, her heart instantly tightening!

That sound... was definitely not a mountain beast; clearly, someone was fighting! And right nearby the Zen courtyard!

Subconsciously, she held her breath, her instinct telling her to retreat back into the room to call for help.

However, her sharp intuition regarding unknown danger made her hold her ground.

Carefully, she crept behind a thick pillar of the corridor, using the shadow of the pillar and the cover of the potted plants on the corridor to anxiously peer toward the source of the sound.

In a small clearing amidst the bamboo grove, a few figures dressed in night-cloaks and masks were fiercely surrounding a man also dressed in profound black, his face half-covered by a ferocious ghostly mask!

The masked man in black moved with astonishing speed, shifting and dodging amid the encirclement of several men. A narrow, elongated curved blade in his hand drew arcs of fatal cold light under the moonlight, every strike carrying piercing murderous intent!

"Pfft!" The dull sound of a blade entering flesh rang out.

One man in black clutched his throat, made a couple of choking sounds, and collapsed limply.

"Form the array!" another man in black barked in a low voice tinged with terror.

The attackers moved with tacit coordination, the flashing blades instantly weaving a net of death, trapping the masked man in black right at the center!

Their offensive was ruthless and tricky, every single move lethal!

Watching this, Qionghua's heart leaped into her throat, her fingers digging tightly into the cold corridor pillar, her fingernails almost sinking into the wood.

She had never witnessed such bloody and cruel slaughter at such close range!

The masked man in black seemed to have been injured as well; his movements paused slightly, and the dark fabric over his left shoulder quickly ripped open to reveal a deeper stain. Yet his momentum grew instead of waning, and he let out a cold snort:

"Shadow Pavilion business. Those who block, die!"

This voice was intentionally suppressed to a deep, hoarse whisper, hard to recognize, yet carrying an authority that chilled one to the bone!

Hearing this, the attacking men in black noticeably paused in their assault. One of them let out an involuntary gasp of disbelief, his voice laden with incredulous terror.

"Shadow Pavilion?! You are... You are the 'Pavilion Master'?!'

This exclamation exploded like a thunderclap in the silent bamboo grove, and in Qionghua's mind as well!

Shadow Pavilion! Pavilion Master!

Even with her reclusive lifestyle, Qionghua had heard of this name.

It was the most mysterious and spine-chilling assassin organization in the pugilistic world. Legend had it that its Pavilion Master came and went like a dragon leaving only its head visible, possessed unfathomable martial arts, and executed ruthless and merciless methods!

Why would he appear in the back mountain of Dazhao Temple? Who were these people? Why were they trying to surround and kill him?

A massive wave of fear gripped Qionghua!

She knew she had stumbled upon an earth-shattering secret!

With this level of bloodshed, either side discovering her presence would undoubtedly result in instant, unhesitating silencing!

She bit down hard on her lower lip, not daring to make a single sound, desperately shrinking herself into the shadow of the pillar, wishing she could turn into a stone.

The battle in the grove had reached its white-hot peak.

The masked man in black wielded a blade like splashing moonlight, wherever it passed, raising showers of blood!

"Ah!"

"Ugh!"

Screams rang out one after another, and the surrounding men in black fell one by one like cut wheat.

In the blink of an eye, only he remained standing in the clearing with his blade, his entire body emanating a dense reek of blood and biting killing intent.

He breathed heavily, and the wound on his left shoulder was clearly having a significant impact.

Qionghua's heart practically stopped beating! She closed her eyes tightly, praying for the other party to leave quickly.

However, things went contrary to her wishes.

The Pavilion Master's blade-like, icy gaze swept across the battlefield with tangible substance, and finally, it locked with absolute precision right onto the corridor pillar where Qionghua was hiding.

chapters.title: That Was Close
chapters.content:
Though separated by a mask, Wen Qionghua felt as though that gaze pierced straight through the shadows and locked firmly onto her! A chill instantly shot from the soles of her feet to the top of her head, and her limbs grew rigid!

The Pavilion Master raised his blade and walked step by step toward the corridor pillar. His footsteps were silent, yet it felt as though he were treading upon the tip of Wen Qionghua's heart. With every step he drew closer, the aura of death grew denser. The moonlight fell upon his ferocious ghost mask and the dripping blood on his curved blade, making him look like a Rakshasa returned from hell.

Wen Qionghua closed her eyes in despair, knowing she could not escape. She could even smell the heavy stench of blood in the air and the icy killing aura emanating from him.

The curved blade lifted, carrying a chilling, gloomy gleam, ready to fall!

At that very moment of imminent peril!

The Pavilion Master's movements stopped abruptly and bizarrely.

Through the eyeholes of the mask, his gaze landed on Wen Qionghua's face, which was slightly upturned in extreme terror.

The moonlight, clear as water, illuminated her face; pale to the point of transparency, her delicate features slightly distorted by fear, long eyelashes trembling like butterfly wings, eyes tightly shut, with a trace of crystal moisture lingering at the corners of her eyes. Fragile, beautiful, panic-stricken, resembling a young deer cornered by a beast at the edge of a cliff.

Those eyes, which had originally been overflowing with killing intent, flashed with a trace of astonishment the moment they clearly registered her face. The tip of his blade trembled slightly, leaving a shallow red scratch across her neck.

Taking advantage of the moment, Wen Qionghua stepped back, but tripped over a bamboo root and fell backward. The man in black instinctively reached out, hooking her waist. That hand was warm and dry, completely different from the icy touch of an assassin she had imagined.

She raised her eyes to meet a pair of orbs, rippling with light, the tails of the eyes upturned slightly, entirely devoid of killing intent now.

Time seemed to freeze for a fraction of a second.

"Miss! Miss, where are you?" Bitao's anxious call drifted from afar, presumably because she found Qionghua missing for too long and had come searching.

The man in black's eyes turned sharp. He raised his hand and gave a light, deft chop to the back of her neck using clever force.

"Ugh..." Wen Qionghua felt a numbness at the back of her neck, unable even to let out an exclamation before her vision went completely black, losing consciousness entirely as she fell softly backward.

Extending an arm, the Pavilion Master steadily caught her softly collapsing body. What filled his arms was a feather-light weight and a delicate fragility palpable even through layers of clothing. He lowered his head, gazing at the breathtakingly beautiful face in his arms, lifeless at the moment, yet still stunning even in unconsciousness, and the brow behind the mask furrowed almost imperceptibly.

He swiftly and gently laid her down in the shadows behind the corridor pillar, ensuring she wouldn't be easily spotted. In the midst of these actions, there was a swiftness, bordering on meticulous care, that stood in stark contrast to his earlier killing.

Having finished all this, he lingered no longer. With a flash of his figure like a ghost blending into the night, he vanished into the depths of the bamboo grove in a few leaps.

When Wen Qionghua woke up again, she was already lying on the bed in her Zen chamber. Liuying and Bitao were standing guard by the bedside, their eyes red and swollen from crying.

"Miss! You're finally awake!" Bitao lunged forward. "You scared the life out of this servant!"

Wen Qionghua propped her upper body up, a dull pain lingering at the back of her neck. "I... what happened to me?"

"Does Miss not remember?" Liuying's voice trembled. "We found you near the Scripture Repository. You had fainted in the bamboo grove, and on your neck... on your neck there was even a bloody scratch!"

Wen Qionghua raised a hand to touch the side of her neck, and sure enough, she felt a thin scratch that had already scabbed over. Memories came rushing back like a tide, the blade of the man in black, those bottomless eyes.

"Did you see anyone else?" she asked urgently.

The two maids shook their heads. "Aside from Miss, we saw nothing."

Wen Qionghua frowned. What about that corpse? Had it been disposed of as well?

"The abbot said Miss probably suffered a fright and needs proper recuperation," Liuying said, tucking the blanket around her. "Let's return to the estate tomorrow. This temple... seems a bit unsafe."

"Why is Miss's complexion so pale?" Bitao said worriedly. "Should we call a doctor?"

"No need," Wen Qionghua forced a smile. "I'm a bit tired. You two can step back first."

After the maids withdrew, Qionghua walked over to the bronze mirror to inspect the scratch on her neck. The cut was extremely fine, showing that the person who struck had clearly exercised restraint. She recalled the brief hesitation of the man in black.

Did he know her?

Even stranger was those eyes... they were inexplicably somewhat familiar. Yet no matter how she searched her memory, she couldn't recall where she might have seen them.

Outside the window, a bright full moon hung high in the sky. Wen Qionghua lightly stroked the scratch on the side of her neck.

What she did not know was that, at the same time, inside a luxurious private room on the top floor of the capital's premier brothel, the "Drunken Immortal Tower," Xie Linyuan was leaning lazily by the window, toying with a wine cup. His robes were half-open, his eyes hazy with drink; anyone looking would take him for nothing more than a thoroughly dissolute prodigal son.

A dancing girl accidentally knocked over a tea set, splashing wine instantly over the left shoulder of the man, who let out an imperceptible grunt of pain.

Lifting the wine cup before him, he tilted his head back and drained it.

A droplet of spilled liquid trickled down his smooth neck into his glowing white chest.

A pair of phoenix eyes narrowed slightly, as if recalling something interesting.

The moonlight filtered through the lattice window, casting mottled shadows across his peerlessly handsome face. In that instant, where was there any trace of a spendthrift?

chapters.title: The Noodle-Selling Brother-in-Law
chapters.content:
As Xie Linfeng adjusted his attire for the fifth time, faint dark circles were already visible beneath his eyes in the bronze mirror. Ever since his father ordered him to make a personal visit to apologize, this simple errand seemed cursed by the plague god, running into setbacks again and again.

Day one. "Young Master, the carriage is ready," the manservant reported softly from outside the door.

Xie Linfeng took a deep breath and smoothed out the last crease on his brocade robe.

When the carriage rolled out of the Xie residence gates, the daylight was just right. Xie Linfeng's tense nerves relaxed slightly as he leaned against the soft cushion and closed his eyes to rest. The rhythmic and steady sound of the wheels crushing the bluestone pavement continued until,

"Crack!"

With a crisp snap, the carriage tilted violently. Caught off guard, Xie Linfeng slammed against the compartment wall, immediately raising a bump on his forehead.

"What's going on?" he demanded, flipping aside the carriage curtain.

"Replying to the Young Master, the wheel... fell off..."

On the second day, he switched to riding a horse. A docile bay horse, usually the most well-behaved of creatures. But just as they reached Vermilion Bird Avenue, the horse suddenly neighed in alarm and reared its front hooves high. Caught unawares, Xie Linfeng was almost thrown from the saddle.
