On the third day, he simply chose to walk. Just as he turned the street corner, a basin of cold water fell from the sky, drenching him thoroughly. An old woman upstairs apologized in a panic, claiming it was a slip of the hand and she didn't know anyone was downstairs.

"What in the world!" Xie Linfeng cursed under his breath, his face as dark as dripping water when he returned to the manor.

On the fourth day, all was calm and peaceful. When he finally stood before the vermilion gates of the Wen residence, a thin layer of cold sweat had already soaked his back.

"Is Miss Wen truly not at the estate?" he asked, forcing down his irritation.

The doorman replied respectfully yet distantly, "Answering the Xie Young Master, Miss has indeed gone to the Great Zhao Temple for quiet cultivation, and her return date is uncertain."

"Please convey my message to Lord Wen; Xie will call upon him another day."

He barely maintained the composure of an aristocratic young master. As he turned to leave, however, he caught a flash of disdain in the doorman's eyes.

An nameless anger flared up in his chest. When had he, Xie Linfeng, ever suffered such idle grievances? By what right did the Wen family look at him with such a gaze? He and Sanniang were completely innocent; it was merely a momentary impulse of compassion...

His thoughts stopped short. Standing in the middle of the street, Xie Linfeng suddenly realized his feet seemed to have a will of their own, walking step by step toward the Eastern Market. He was startled to realize that since that day, he hadn't visited the noodle shop for several days.

The sign for "Liu's Noodle Shop" swayed gently in the wind. The shop door was half-closed, with a wooden sign hanging outside reading "Closed for Business." Xie Linfeng's heart tightened as he pushed the door open.

"Miss Liu?" Xie Linfeng called out. No one answered.

He lifted the fabric curtain and walked into the back room, only to see Sanniang squatting at the door of the inner chamber, packing her luggage. She wore a half-worn lotus-pink blouse, with only a wooden hairpin securing her hair, and several tied bundles piled by her feet. Hearing footsteps, she jerked her head up, tears still pooled in her swollen eyes.

"Y-Young Master?" Sanniang hastily wiped her face with her sleeve. "Why are you here..."

Xie Linfeng felt as though his chest had been struck by something. He strode forward. "Has someone been bullying you?" His voice was taut with a tension he hadn't realized was there. His first reaction was Wen Qionghua, but then he remembered she wasn't even in the capital right now. Could it be his father? Or the Wen family?

"No!" Sanniang shook her head repeatedly. "No one is bullying me. It's just... I've learned the identity of that young lady." She gave a bitter smile. "If I continue to stay here, I will only bring you endless trouble."

"The silver I owe you, I will slowly pay back." Sanniang pulled a coarse cloth money pouch from her bosom, holding it up with both hands. "This is what I've saved over the past two months, although it's not much..."

"Nonsense!" Xie Linfeng pressed down on her hands. "You actually believe those idle gossip rumors? My affair with Miss Wen has nothing to do with you! Since this shop was given to you, it is yours!"

Sanniang's hands were as cold as snow, trembling slightly in his palms. "It does matter, Xie Young Master." Her eyes were swimming with tears. "Though I am of humble birth, I still know propriety, righteousness, and shame. You have treated me with grace as heavy as a mountain; how could I... how could I bring you into disrepute?"

Looking at the stubborn eyes of the person before him, he unconsciously recalled another pair of peerlessly beautiful yet cold eyes. Driven by some inexplicable impulse, he actually pulled Sanniang into his embrace.

Sanniang stiffened in his arms for a split second, then burst into tears. Having lost her mother at a young age, with her father just passing away and her two older brothers good for nothing, when had anyone ever treated her with such gentleness? In this embrace filled with the scent of sandalwood, she finally shed all her defenses and sobbed like a wronged child.

Not until a tear fell onto the back of Xie Linfeng's neck did he snap back to his senses and realize she was already in his arms. He struggled for a brief moment, yet ultimately did not let go.

Outside the door, a dark shadow flashed past soundlessly.

---

West City, Good Fortune Gambling House.

In the bustling, clamorous hall, two ragged men were pinned down onto a gambling table, their faces bruised and battered.

"Let go of me!" one of them struggled and cursed. "Do you know who my brother-in-law is? Hearing it will scare you to death!"

A thug sneered, grabbing him by the hair and slamming his face hard against the table top. "You scoundrel, who are you trying to drag into this?"

Seeing this, the other man shrieked at the top of his lungs, "You know Liu's Noodle Shop in the Eastern Market, right? That's opened by my younger sister! Behind her stands the Second Young Master of the Prime Minister's Estate, Xie! If you dare touch us, Young Master Xie won't let you off!"

The gambling house fell silent for a fraction of a second, followed by an outbreak of roaring laughter.

"Xie's Second Young Master?" The thug exaggeratedly picked his ear. "With your sorry lot, you think you're worthy of claiming kinship with the Xie family?"

"It's true! Go ask around if you don't believe it!" Liu Da shouted loudly. "Xie's Second Young Master took a fancy to my sister! Just a few days ago, he protected her even against the nobles of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate! Soon, I'll be the brother-in-law of the Xie family!"

The gambling house went dead still. The thugs looked at each other, and the strength in their grip involuntarily loosened by three tenths.

On the second-floor private room, pearl curtains rustled. A tipsy voice drifted down; it belonged to an extraordinarily handsome man in red, with a seductive tear mole beneath his eye. "Oh? When did Xie's Second Young Master acquire a noodle-selling brother-in-law?"

"It's as true as gold!" Liu Er said, his eyes red with anxiety. "Xie's Second Young Master has taken a shine to my sister! A few days ago, he even protected her right in front of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate's young lady! The whole Eastern Market knows about this!"

"Xie Linfeng could fall for your sister? A toad trying to eat swan meat!" Another man's voice alongside the red-robed man rang out.

Seeing someone question him, Liu Da immediately grew anxious. "What kind of thing are you?! My sister is a pure and untarnished maiden; Xie's Second Young Master comes to her shop to eat noodles every single day, if that's not fancying her, what is it?!"

"Exactly!" Liu Er chimed in. "A few days ago, that young lady from the Xuanhe Prince's Estate even came specifically to pick a fight! If it weren't for Xie's Second Young Master protecting her..."

The red-robed man's gaze turned cold, and the wine cup in his hand shattered with a "clink" on the floor. The entire hall fell silent.

"Interesting." Swaying as he walked downstairs, the jade pendant at his waist jingled crisply. "Then tell me, how did Xie's Second Young Master 'protect' your sister?"

Believing he had the upper hand, Liu Da piled on the exaggeration. "That prince's estate young lady threw her weight around and insisted my sister kneel on the spot to apologize! Xie's Second Young Master stepped right up, pulled my sister straight into his arms, and said..."

"And what did he say?" The red-robed man's voice was frighteningly gentle.

"He said... he said his heart holds only my sister, and told that sickly wench to give up and die early!" Liu Er rushed to answer, looking immensely smug. "The neighbors all saw it!"

The red-robed man suddenly smiled, a brilliance so dazzling it made one's hair stand on end. "Interesting." He straightened up and told the manager, "Put their debts on my tab."

Liu Da and Liu Er were overjoyed and about to kowtow in gratitude when they heard this dissolute young master add airily: "Lend them another five hundred taels."

The manager understood immediately, and promptly ordered his men to bring over the gaming chips. Bending down to whisper in Liu Da's ear, his breath reeked of wine mixed with pine wood: "Bet more... once your sister becomes Madame Xie, what amount of silver can't be repaid?"

The red-robed man turned and walked back toward the second-floor private room, all trace of drunkenness gone from his face. The dark shadow beside him followed silently: "Master, should those two be dealt with?"

"No need." The man sneered. "Let them spread it. The more absurd the rumors, the better." He pushed open the window and gazed in the direction of the Great Zhao Temple.

chapters.title: First Meeting
chapters.content:
On the mountain path of the Great Zhao Temple, a procession of carriages moved slowly forward. Wen Qionghua leaned inside the cushion-lined carriage.

The interior was scented with calming aloeswood. Qionghua half-reclined against a soft pillow, her slender fingers gently massaging her temples. These past few days of quiet temple cultivation should have restored her spirit, but she remained unsettled due to the assassin from that night.

"Miss, we will reach the capital in another two hours," Liuying reported softly, handing her a cup of warm ginseng tea.

Just as Qionghua reached to take it, the carriage suddenly lurched, and the ginseng tea almost spilled. From outside came the driver's shouts to rein in the horses and a burst of commotion.

"What is going on?" Bitao lifted a corner of the carriage curtain.

Ahead of them lay a damaged carriage, with three servant-like figures busy bustling around a broken wheel. Seeing the Wen family carriage halt, one of them hurriedly stepped forward to bow. "We have disturbed the noble ones! My young master drank to the point of passing out, yet unfortunately his carriage axle snapped, and with evening approaching..."

Liuying frowned. "Step aside then. What does that have to do with us?"

The servant bowed repeatedly. "It's truly... truly because we fear the young master will sleep out in the wilderness and meet with an accident. We beg the noble ones to show mercy and give us a convenience, asking if you might offer our young master a ride."

Qionghua originally had no intention of paying attention, but the moment she lifted the curtain, she caught sight of the Xie family crest hanging from the wrecked carriage. Her fingertips paused slightly, her gaze lingering for a moment on that Azure Bird family emblem.

"Let him up," she said flatly, her voice devoid of emotion. "Have him sit in the rear carriage."

The servant expressed profuse gratitude and retreated. Before long, two footmen came stumbling along, supporting a man dressed in red. The man possessed a slender build, a flamboyant red robe draped loosely over him, exposing a large expanse of jade-like chest. His long, raven-dark hair was bound casually with a golden ribbon, and several strands of loose hair hung over his forehead, swaying gently with his unsteady steps.

"I won't ride in that broken cart in the back..." The red-robed man suddenly shook off the footmen, pointing drunkenly at Qionghua's carriage. "I... I want to ride this one! This one is pretty!"

Without further ado, he began scrambling up onto Qionghua's carriage. Liuying and Bitao were struck pale with shock and moved to stop him, only to see their young mistress give a slight wave of her hand.

The red-robed man stumbled blindly into the carriage compartment, carrying with him a strong wave of alcoholic reek. Qionghua covered her nose with a handkerchief, her beautiful brows slightly furrowed. Unaware of it entirely, the man slumped onto the opposite seat and hazily raised his face...

A face so stunning it bordered on the demonic abruptly entered her line of sight.

Qionghua's breathing hitched. Though she considered herself handsome, she had never laid eyes upon such a soul-captivating appearance. The man's skin was as white as snow, his brows like ink paintings, his nose high and straight, and his lips like painted vermilion. Most alluring of all were those slightly upturned phoenix eyes, with a single tear mole at the outer corner acting as the finishing touch, making his entire face appear both bewitching and gorgeous. At present, it was flushed faintly red from drink, adding a hint of dissolute charm. Yet those eyes felt inexplicably familiar.

"Fairy..." the red-robed man stared at her infatuatedly, his voice husky with intoxication. "Have I... arrived at the Moon Palace?"

"I am Wen Qionghua," Qionghua said calmly, her gaze roving over his face. "You must be the eldest young master of the Xie family, right?"

The red-robed gentleman, Xie Linyuan, flashed an imperceptible trace of clarity in his eyes upon hearing this, which was instantly swallowed back by drunkenness. Dragging out his syllables with seven parts intoxication and three parts mockery, he drawled, "So it's Wen~ Big~ Miss~ after all~ What a coincidence... such a coincidence..."

He deliberately pronounced the four words "Wen Big Miss" with endless turns, the ending note lifting upward with an unspeakable frivolousness.

Qionghua ignored him further and closed her eyes to rest. Finding no amusement, Xie Linyuan lazily leaned back against the carriage wall, though a pair of phoenix eyes traced the young lady opposite him without leaving a trace.

Her porcelain-white skin was nearly transparent, with faint dark shadows beneath her eyes, clearly showing she hadn't rested well. A scabbed wound scarred the side of her neck, looking like an imperfection upon the snow, glaringly harsh to the eye.

As the carriage rolled slowly forward, the only sounds inside the compartment for a time were Xie Linyuan's tune-less humming and the crunch of wheels over stones. Though Qionghua kept her eyes closed, she could sense that tangible gaze lingering continuously on her face. She suddenly felt some regret for letting this dissolute scoundrel board her carriage.

The carriage suddenly jolted again.

"Whoosh..."

The sound of air tearing open rang out abruptly, followed immediately by the dull thud of an arrow embedding itself into wood.

"Assassins! Protect the Miss!" Outside, utter chaos instantly broke out, with the clashing of weapons and shouts mingling together.

Qionghua kept her eyes closed, not even fluttering her eyelashes. But Xie Linyuan shrank back violently, diving directly behind her and instinctively reaching to grab her sleeve. "S-Save me! There are bad guys!"

Finally opening her eyes, Wen Qionghua turned to look at him in disbelief.

This Xie eldest young master had scurried to her side like a frightened rabbit, his entire body nearly shrinking into her arms. That bewitching face was written over with terror, acting exactly like a startled hare, where was any trace of his earlier frivolousness?

Wen Qionghua: "..."

Expressionless, she yanked her sleeve back. "Young Master Xie, please exercise self-respect."

Undeterred, Xie Linyuan pressed close again. "Miss Wen, swords and blades have no eyes outside..."

"Young Master Xie," she pulled her sleeve back leisurely, "the Wen family guards are well-trained. You can rest easy."

Yet Xie Linyuan trembled even more violently. "I... I'm scared..."

Staring fixedly at him, Wen Qionghua suddenly leaned forward. The distance between them shrank abruptly, close enough for her to see her own reflection in his pupils. Xie Linyuan's breathing hitched as he instinctively leaned back, only to be blocked by the carriage wall.

"Young Master Xie," Wen Qionghua's voice was as soft as a feather brushing an earlobe, "you reek of alcohol, yet there is not the slightest trace of liquor on your breath."

Her fingertip tapped lightly against his chest. "Furthermore, your heartbeat is steady, completely lacking the rapid pulse a drunkard should have... Truly interesting."

Xie Linyuan's pupils contracted slightly.

"What's more coincidental," Wen Qionghua continued, "is that though Qionghua rarely goes out, I seldom encounter assassins. The moment I share a carriage with Young Master Xie today..."

The fighting outside came to an abrupt halt. Liuying reported from outside the carriage, "Miss, the assassins have all been dealt with, and the surviving captives have been sent to the Eldest Young Master for interrogation."

With a bland "Mmm," Qionghua leaned back against her soft cushion once more, as if the assassination attempt just now were merely an inconsequential interlude. She looked at Xie Linyuan, who was still huddled in the corner, the corners of her lips curling upward. "When does Young Master Xie plan to stop pretending?"

Silence hung inside the carriage for a moment. Xie Linyuan shrank back further behind her. "I spilled wine on my clothes just to escape the drinking!" His tone remained frivolous, yet carried a hint of elusive meaning. "As for the assassins... it's also my first time encountering them, I was scared to death..."

The final syllable lifted upward with deliberate coquettishness. Qionghua nearly laughed in exasperation, this person... what a thick skin!

"Fortunately, I met Miss Wen~" Xie Linyuan suddenly leaned closer, that bewitching face magnifying in Qionghua's vision. "Miss Wen is my great savior~"

Qionghua slapped him squarely on the forehead, shoving him away. "If Young Master Xie comes any closer, I don't mind making you truly 'scared to death'."

Clutching his forehead, Xie Linyuan shrunk back with a pitiful expression. "Miss Wen is so fierce..." Despite his words, a trace of warmth flashed in his eyes.

chapters.title: Mutual Probing
chapters.content:
Wen Qionghua couldn't be bothered to pick apart his clumsy act and sat up straight again.

"Resume the journey," Wen Qionghua instructed faintly, closing her eyes once more to rest.

Xie Linyuan wouldn't stay still, however: "Miss Wen is so formidable. Not a single expression changes even when encountering an assassination attempt." He tilted his head to appraise her.

Qionghua didn't even open her eyes: "Since Young Master Xie is so concerned, could it be that you know the inside story?"

"How could I possibly know!" Xie Linyuan waved his hands exaggeratedly. "I'm just a dissolute playboy who lives off his family... But..." He suddenly leaned closer, lowering his voice, "If Miss Qionghua is willing to grace me with her company for a cup of wine, I might just be able to help you investigate..."

Qionghua finally opened her eyes, looking at him with a half-smile: "Is Young Master Xie... trying to blackmail me?"

"How dare I, how dare I!" Xie Linyuan smiled as harmlessly as a domestic animal. "I just wanted to make friends with Miss Wen~"

Friends? Qionghua sneered inwardly. A notorious son of a concubine, and a noblewoman whose engagement was about to be broken off; what kind of pure friendship could they possibly have? Furthermore...

Her gaze swept over Xie Linyuan's hand, which seemed to be draped casually over his knee; those slender fingers had distinct knuckles, and the webbing between his thumb and index finger possessed a layer of light calluses, the kind left behind by gripping a sabre year round. How could a playboy who indulged in wine and women all day long have such calluses on his hands?

"Young Master Xie," she spoke suddenly, "I heard that Second Young Master Xie has been getting rather close to a certain Miss Liu lately?"

Xie Linyuan's expression faltered for a fraction of a second, then his smile grew even more brilliant: "That younger brother of mine... truly has a unique taste. Rejecting a beauty like Miss Wen and instead taking a fancy to some wild flower from the marketplace."

"Is that so?" Qionghua gently tapped her fingertips against the handwarmer. "I actually find that Miss Liu... rather special."

Xie Linyuan narrowed his eyes: "Is Miss Wen... jealous?"

Qionghua chuckled softly: "Young Master Xie jests. I was simply curious..." She raised her eyes, her gaze sharp as a blade. "If Second Young Master Xie insists on marrying that Miss Liu, how will Prime Minister Xie react?"

The temperature inside the carriage plummeted. The smile on Xie Linyuan's face faded slightly: "Miss Wen seems very concerned about my brother's marriage prospects?"

"Just asking in passing," Qionghua leaned back against the soft cushions again. "After all... my engagement to the Xie family has not yet been annulled."

Xie Linyuan's pupils constricted slightly. He stared at Qionghua for a long time, then suddenly put back on that flippant, irreverent smile: "If Miss Wen truly marries into the Xie family, wouldn't that make you call me 'Eldest Brother'?" He deliberately dragged out his tone. "Just thinking about it makes me rather look forward to it~"

Qionghua didn't take the bait, simply watching him perform in silence.

An eerie silence fell inside the carriage. Xie Linyuan tilted his head to study Qionghua and suddenly asked: "The wound on Miss Wen's neck... how did you get it?"

Qionghua's fingertips paused, then she nonchalantly adjusted her collar: "Scratched by a cat."

"Oh?" Xie Linyuan raised an eyebrow. "What cat is so bold that it dares to scratch the Wen family's little phoenix?"

"Just a stray cat," Qionghua had no desire to elaborate. "Young Master Xie would do better to worry about your own predicament. I will report today's events truthfully to my father."

Xie Linyuan's smile remained unchanged: "Quite right, quite right~ But..." He suddenly lowered his voice, "Is Miss Wen truly not curious about who those assassins were targeting?"

Qionghua finally looked him in the eye: "Young Master Xie knows?"

"How could I~" Xie Linyuan blinked. "I meant to say that since Miss Wen is so stunning, perhaps some blind fool has set his sights on you..."

"Young Master Xie," Qionghua interrupted coldly.

Xie Linyuan raised both hands in a gesture of surrender: "Alright, alright, we won't talk about that." He suddenly smiled mysteriously, "However... if Miss Wen doesn't want to marry my brother, I happen to have an idea..."

Qionghua raised an eyebrow at him.

"Marry me~" Xie Linyuan smiled with complete lack of care. "We're all Xie sons anyway, what difference does it make which one you marry? Though my reputation is a bit poor, I am good-looking, after all~"

Qionghua stared at him for a long while, then suddenly smiled as well. That smile was like melting ice and snow, breathtakingly beautiful, yet it sent a chill down Xie Linyuan's spine.

Qionghua didn't even lift her eyelids: "Young Master Xie."

"Hmm?"

"Your hand."

Xie Linyuan looked down and discovered that at some point, he had grabbed her sleeve again, his fingertips even seductively caressing the fine cloud-patterned brocade. He sheepishly let go, though without showing much remorse: "Miss Wen's dress material is fine, it feels comfortable to touch."

Qionghua finally opened her eyes, those autumn-water-like eyes gazing straight at him: "Young Master Xie's appearance here today, was it truly just a coincidence?"

Xie Linyuan blinked and suddenly leaned in close, so close that he could see his own reflection in her eyes. "What does Miss Wen think?" His voice suddenly dropped, carrying a trace of dangerous allure. "Could it be... that I came here specifically to abduct a beauty?"

Crack!

The folding fan in Qionghua's hand gave his forehead a firm yet light tap. "If you're drunk, behave yourself."

"Xie Linyuan," she said slowly, "do you know why I've been able to live this long?"

Xie Linyuan was startled.

"Because I never meddle in other people's business," Qionghua leaned back against the soft pillow and closed her eyes again. "Especially... the staged business directed and acted by certain people."

Xie Linyuan's smile froze on his face. He stared at Qionghua's calm sleeping face, his gaze deepening. This Miss Wen was far more intelligent than he had anticipated...

Without opening her eyes, Qionghua's lips curved slightly: "Let's hope that next time, Young Master Xie can come up with a fresher trick."

The carriage suddenly halted, and Liuying's voice came from outside: "Milady, we've reached the city gate."

Xie Linyuan switched back to his flippant expression and smacked his lips regretfully: "We're here already? I wanted to spend a bit more time talking with Miss Wen~"

Wen Qionghua made no comment. Xie Linyuan cheerfully jumped off the carriage, and before leaving, he didn't forget to turn back and cast a wink: "Thank you for saving me today, Miss Wen. Another day, Xie will certainly call upon you to express his gratitude."

"No need," Qionghua said faintly. "Merely a matter of convenience."

"It is needed, it is needed~" Xie Linyuan resumed his dissolute demeanor. "I heard that Miss Wen is well-versed in the zither. Though I am untalented, I happen to have collected a few ancient zithers. Another day, I shall bring them for Miss Wen to appreciate..."

Qionghua finally gave him a proper look: "Young Master Xie."

"Hmm?"

"You have eye discharge at the corner of your eye."

"......"

When the Xie family's servant boy arrived to pick him up, what he saw was his own eldest young master wearing a defeated expression, while faint suppressed feminine laughter drifted from inside the carriage.

Once the Wen family's carriage had distanced itself, the drunkenness on Xie Linyuan's face vanished instantly. Standing in the shadow of the street corner, he watched the direction where the luxurious carriage had disappeared, his fingertips unconsciously rubbing the spot on his sleeve where he had touched her earlier.

"Master," Moying appeared silently, "the person has been dealt with."

Xie Linyuan gave a soft hum. Lost in thought, Moying asked: "Did Master manage to investigate the matter from that day?"

Xie Linyuan replied calmly: "She shouldn't be aware of it. However..." Some people still needed to be kept under his own nose to give him peace of mind.

Gazing at the gradually illuminating lights outside the window, Xie Linyuan softly murmured, "Miss Wen, we will meet again."

chapters.title: Who Would Dare to Show Off in Front of Wen Qionghua?
chapters.content:
Inside the Xuanhe Prince's Estate, the scent of medicine hung thick in Qionghua Pavilion.

Wen Qionghua lay propped against a pile of brocade quilts and soft pillows, her face even paler than the plain satin beneath her.

Ever since she returned from the ambush outside the capital, she had been ill for several more days, coughing without pause, looking more delicate and fragile than ever. Her whole family was sick with worry, and good things flowed toward her in a steady stream.

Spring sunshine filled the world outside her window, yet she had no desire even to step out of her courtyard.

"Miss, the gatekeeper says the Xie family's Second Young Master came by once a few days ago, and when he heard you were not receiving visitors, he never came again." Liuying came in carrying the medicine bowl and reported carefully.

Qionghua's expression stayed indifferent. She did not even lift her eyelids. "Oh."

She had long since made up her mind to have nothing more to do with Xie Linfeng.

She was the only legitimate daughter of three generations of the Wen family, raised in the palm of everyone's hand. Since childhood, who had ever dared to give her the slightest grievance?

Yet Xie Linfeng had publicly humiliated her for the sake of a woman who sold noodles.

It was not that she refused to hold it against him. It was that the very thought of it made her feel especially sick, and even seeing the man's face would make her physically ill.

All she wanted now was to kick him out of any connection whatsoever with Wen Qionghua, and quickly.

She remembered the eyes of the black-clad assassin that night, and the bewitching face of Xie Linyuan in the carriage on the way back.

"Xie Linyuan..." she murmured the name without realizing it.

"What did you say, Miss?" Liuying hadn't heard clearly.

"Nothing." Qionghua took the bowl and drained it in one gulp, frowning. "Hasn't Grandfather come back yet?"

"Not yet. They say he has reached Mount Hua and will probably enjoy himself there for a while longer," Bitao answered. "If the Old Prince learned that you had suffered such an insult..."

"Don't tell Grandfather for now. It's rare for him to be enjoying himself so much," Wen Qionghua said lazily.

As for Xie Linfeng, she would avoid him as far as possible.

But this Xie Linyuan seemed strange in every way.

His looks were certainly excellent. It was only that... there was something faintly odd about him...

While she was still thinking, Liuying hurried in holding a gold-embossed invitation. "Miss, an invitation to Princess Ningshuang's coming-of-age banquet."

Qionghua took the card, her fingertip brushing over its delicate cloud patterns. Princess Ningshuang was one of her few friends. Though the legitimate daughter of the Emperor and Empress, she was carefree and lively by nature, and fiercely protective of her own. This banquet, Qionghua could not skip.

"Prepare a gift," Qionghua said with a couple of light coughs. "If I don't go, that girl will nag me about it for half a year."

Liuying was full of worry. "But with the Miss's cough..."

"It won't kill me." Qionghua waved a hand. "I heard the Empress will be there too?"

"Yes," Bitao nodded. "The Princess is the Empress's own daughter, so of course her coming-of-age ceremony will be grand."

Wen Qionghua's eyes flickered. The Empress had been a close friend of her mother's since their girlhood and treated her like her own daughter.

As for the matter of breaking the engagement, if she could first drop a hint to the Empress...

---

The Princess's Mansion was hung with lanterns and festoons, and the fine carriages and horses of noble ladies lined half the street.

Wen Qionghua's carriage arrived last of all, yet no one dared say a word. The gatekeeper, seeing the crest of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate, hurried forward to lead the way.

She wore a moon-white gown embroidered with silver-thread butterflies, covered by a pale green gauze robe, with only a white jade magnolia hairpin in her hair, so simple it was almost plain. Yet as she stepped slowly down from the carriage on Liuying's arm, all the spring colors of the garden seemed to dim.

"Qionghua!" The moment Princess Ningshuang saw her, she lifted her skirts and ran over, linking arms with her affectionately. "You've finally come! I thought you were going to shirk again!"

Qionghua smiled faintly. "Your coming-of-age ceremony, Princess. How could I dare not come?"

Princess Ningshuang looked her up and down and frowned. "Why have you gotten thinner again? Your color isn't good either. Are you sick again?"

Qionghua shook her head. "It's nothing. The old trouble."

Ningshuang leaned close to her ear and lowered her voice. "I heard about the wonderful thing that scoundrel Xie Linfeng did! Do you want me to get revenge for you?"

Qionghua covered her mouth with a couple of light coughs and shook her head. "No need. Why waste effort on someone of no consequence?"

"You..." Ningshuang poked her forehead helplessly. "You're just too good-natured!"

The two went into the banquet arm in arm, and all along the way the glances of the noble ladies, some open and some veiled, followed them like shadows.

Qionghua seemed not to notice, and only talked quietly with the Princess.

"Look, that sickly invalid of the Wen family has come too."

"I heard Young Master Xie ignored even her dignity for the sake of a woman who sells noodles. How does she still have the face to go out?"

"Shh, keep your voice down! She's the apple of the Prince of Xuanhe's eye. Do you want to die?"

Princess Ningshuang's face darkened, and she was about to lose her temper, but Qionghua gently pressed her hand. "No need."

"They dare to talk about you like that!" Princess Ningshuang puffed with anger. "This Princess will get revenge for you!"

Qionghua laughed softly. "Who could possibly anger me?" Her gaze swept over the noble ladies whispering not far away, and they immediately fell silent and pretended to admire the flowers in the garden.

That was true enough. These people only dared to grumble sourly behind her back to satisfy their tongues. In family background or in looks and talent, was there any way in which Wen Qionghua was not at the very top? They only dared to gossip about her frailty. Who would be sick of living enough to show off in front of Wen Qionghua herself!

Seeing that she did not mind, Princess Ningshuang could say nothing more. She only glared fiercely at that group of ladies and pulled Qionghua to her seat.

On the men's side, Xie Linfeng, in an indigo brocade robe, his face cold and noble, was exchanging courtesies with several young masters of prominent families. The moment he appeared, he drew the frequent glances of quite a few noble ladies.

"Young Master Xie the Second is truly without peer. That Wen Qionghua relies on her good family to monopolize such a gentleman."

"Exactly. A pretty face and nothing else, and a sickly invalid at that. How is she worthy of Young Master Xie the Second?" another agreed.

"Just wait. There will be a good show today," said a noble lady in a pink dress, gazing at Xie Linfeng in a daze and smiling meaningfully. Her eyes held only foolish glee, and she had completely forgotten that this was a banquet hosted by the Empress's own daughter!

Qionghua sat among the guests, lowered her head to sip some tea, and hid a trace of weariness in her eyes.

So noisy, so tiring, no strength...

Halfway through the banquet, a commotion suddenly rose at the side gate.

A servant was leading in a woman carrying a shoulder pole. She wore coarse cloth clothing and had a plain, pleasant face, but her expression was full of fear. Her head was bowed and her fingers clutched the hem of her clothes tightly. She was clearly unaccustomed to such an occasion.

"Liu Sanniang?" someone exclaimed.

Qionghua looked up, her brows drawing together slightly.

"What is going on?" Princess Ningshuang asked, displeased.

The noble lady in pink covered her mouth with a light laugh. "Your Highness, I arranged this specially. I heard Miss Liu makes excellent noodles, so I invited her today to show the ladies her skill."

As she spoke, her gaze slid meaningfully toward Wen Qionghua.

The whole room buzzed. The noble lady in pink was none other than Xie Linfeng's cousin, Su Wanrou.

Wen Qionghua's expression did not change. Only her fingertip tapped lightly on her teacup.

Liu Sanniang stood frozen, at a loss. She had been busy at her shop when a few servants had forcibly brought her here, saying that a noble person had named her to make noodles. She had not dared refuse, but never imagined it would be at an occasion like this.

"Miss Liu, why are you standing there?" Su Wanrou said with a smile. "Quickly make a bowl of plain noodle soup for Miss Wen. She is Young Master Xie the Second's fiancée, after all. Shouldn't you serve her well?"

Every word was laced with humiliation.

Liu Sanniang's face turned deathly pale, and she bit her lip, not daring to raise her head.

Qionghua set down her teacup, her voice soft yet unquestionable. "That won't be necessary."

Su Wanrou raised an eyebrow. "What does Miss Wen mean by that? Do you look down on her cooking?"

Qionghua glanced at her lightly. "A banquet at the Princess's Mansion has its own imperial chefs to handle it. Why trouble a woman of the marketplace?"

Su Wanrou, cowed by that gaze, was momentarily speechless.

"Miss Wen..." Liu Sanniang's voice trembled. "I... I didn't..."

Qionghua slowly rose and walked to Liu Sanniang. She stood almost half a head taller than Liu Sanniang, and now she lowered her eyes slightly to look at her. "Miss Liu, there is no need to be afraid."

Seeing the trembling woman before her, she softened her tone. "You may go home. What happened today has nothing to do with you."

Liu Sanniang's eyes reddened slightly. She murmured her thanks and was about to withdraw when a cold voice sounded:

"Miss Wen certainly has great airs."

Everyone turned and saw Xie Linfeng standing at the entrance to the women's seats, though when he had arrived, no one knew, his face dark.

chapters.title: What a Pair of "Star-Crossed Lovers"
chapters.content:
Xie Linfeng, dressed in a blue brocade robe with a face as cold as jade, strode forward and blocked Liu Sanniang's path. He looked coldly at Wen Qionghua, "If Miss Wen has anger in her heart, she can take it out on me. Why make things difficult for an innocent woman?"

Wen Qionghua looked at him quietly, finding it simply ridiculous.

Before she could speak, Princess Ningshuang had already slapped the table and stood up! "Xie Linfeng! You are audacious! When has Qionghua ever made things difficult for her? Clearly, Su Wanrou deliberately brought this person here to humiliate Qionghua. Are you blind?"

Xie Linfeng acted as if he had heard nothing, his eyes filled with disgust as he stared at the stunning beauty before him: "Wen Qionghua, how much longer are you going to put on an act? Sending people to humiliate Sanniang wasn't enough, and now you publicly disgrace her? Is this the upbringing of your Wen family?"

The entire room fell silent. Everyone held their breath, waiting to watch this good show.

Qionghua laughed instead of getting angry: "Young Master Xie is quite mistaken. First, I was not the one who invited Miss Liu; it was your good cousin." She glanced at Su Wanrou, whose face had turned the color of dirt. "Second, I just now ordered servants to prepare a carriage to send Miss Liu back. Where on earth is the talk of disgrace?"

"Specious arguments!" Xie Linfeng sneered. "This isn't the first or second time your Wen family has used power to bully others! The gatekeeper gives me attitude, your older brother repeatedly comes to my door to provoke, and now..."

"It wasn't Miss Wen! This Miss Su called me here!" Liu Sanniang suddenly shouted loudly.

Xie Linfeng paused, looking at Liu Sanniang in disbelief.

Su Wanrou hurriedly defended herself: "Cousin, I just... I just wanted her to make a bowl of noodles for Miss Wen, I didn't mean anything else..."

"Enough," Qionghua said softly, her tone terrifyingly calm.

She raised her eyes to look at Xie Linfeng, a mocking curve at the corners of her lips: "Second Young Master Xie, the betrothal between you and me was originally the command of our elders. If you are unwilling, you could have just said so directly. Why make a public spectacle of embarrassing me time and again for the sake of outsiders?"

Xie Linfeng was left speechless by her question, his brow simply locked in a deep frown.

Wen Qionghua no longer looked at him; she turned to Princess Ningshuang and said, "Your Highness, I am feeling unwell. I take my leave first."

Princess Ningshuang panicked: "Qionghua! Don't leave! It is clearly their fault!"

Qionghua shook her head, gently patted the princess's hand, and signaled that there was no need to say any more.

Just as she took a step forward, Xie Linfeng suddenly blocked her: "Miss Wen, today's matter was my misunderstanding. I apologize to you."

Qionghua paused her steps, lifted her eyes to look at him, her gaze as cold and indifferent as frost: "Second Young Master Xie, I have no need for your apology."

Her voice was very soft, yet every word was crystal clear: "Between you and me, there was never any connection to begin with."

With that, she bypassed him and prepared to walk straight away.

Xie Linfeng stood in place, looking at her retreating back. An unprecedented panic suddenly surged into his heart.

Driven by an impulse he couldn't explain, he grabbed Wen Qionghua's arm. Caught off guard, Wen Qionghua almost stumbled.

"Xie Linfeng!" Princess Ningshuang was furious. "You are insolent! This is Her Highness's residence, not a place for you to run wild!"

Only then did Xie Linfeng realize he had lost his composure. He hurriedly let go and forced a bow: "Forgive me, Your Highness. This subject acted on a sudden impulse..."

"Such a fine 'sudden impulse'!" A dignified voice interrupted harshly. "For Young Master Xie to rage on behalf of a beauty, truly touching indeed."

Xie Linfeng froze all over. Only then did he notice that the Empress on the phoenix throne not far away was eyeing this side coldly.

Qionghua had already turned to face the Empress, bowing gracefully: "Forgive me, Your Empress, for disturbing your good mood."

The Empress's expression eased slightly: "Rise. Qionghua, come here to my side."

Just as Qionghua was about to walk over, Liu Sanniang suddenly dropped to her knees with a thud: "Forgive me, Your Grace! It was all this humble maid's fault! This humble maid will leave right now, I beg you not to blame Young Master Xie..."

Xie Linfeng rushed to help her up with a heart full of distress: "Sanniang, you don't need to..."

"Enough!" the Empress finally spoke, her voice carrying an unangered majesty. "Second Young Master Xie, as a man from outside, breaking into the female guests' quarters is already a grave disrespect. Now you lose your composure in public for a woman of the marketplace, placing Qionghua where? Placing the dignity of the Wen and Xie families where?"

Xie Linfeng's face turned ashen; he knelt to plead for punishment.

The Empress swept a cold glance at him, then her expression softened as she turned back to Qionghua: "Qionghua, what do you think of this matter?"

Qionghua looked at Xie Linfeng and Liu Sanniang kneeling on the ground, suddenly finding it all absurd beyond measure. She coughed twice lightly and said indifferently, "Since Young Master Xie and Miss Liu are of one mind and deeply in love, Qionghua is willing to help fulfill a good match."

The entire assembly gasped in an uproar. These words were practically calling off the engagement in public!

The Empress frowned slightly: "Qionghua..."

"Your Grace," Qionghua bowed gracefully, "Qionghua is truly feeling unwell. I take my leave first."

She turned and left, her back as straight as green bamboo. Xie Linfeng stared blankly after her, suddenly feeling as though a piece of his heart had hollowed out.

Just as Qionghua walked a few steps, a smiling voice suddenly came from the moon gate: "Yo, so lively here?"

A person walked in lazily, twirling a folding fan. His gaze swept around the faces of the crowd before finally landing on Qionghua: "Miss Wen, long time no see~"

The newcomer wore red robes and possessed a face so stunning it bordered on the demonic. His skin was like jade, his lips looked as though stained with vermilion, and a tear mole at the corner of his right eye added a touch of flirtatious charm. It caused the aristocratic maidens present to flush red with embarrassment.

Qionghua paused her steps, meeting those smiling peach-blossom eyes. For some reason, she felt even more a headache coming on than when facing Xie Linfeng.

"Eldest Young Master Xie," she forced a nod.

Xie Linfeng's brother, Xie Linyuan, had already crowded right up to her. He snapped his fan shut, pointed at the pair of "star-crossed lovers" on the ground, and feigned surprise: "Which play is this? The Story of the Western Wing or The Peony Pavilion?"

Qionghua couldn't help but shoot him a sidelong glance: "As for your younger brother's private affairs, Eldest Young Master Xie should ask him."

Just as she was about to leave, her wrist was gently caught by Xie Linyuan. In full view of the crowd, he leaned down and whispered in her ear, his warm breath brushing against her earlobe: "Miss Wen just said she wanted to call off the engagement? What a coincidence, I happen to be missing a wife..."

Qionghua abruptly pulled back her hand, the tips of her ears slightly red: "Xie Linyuan! You..."

"What about me?" Xie Linyuan looked utterly innocent. "An unmarried man and an unmarried woman, with such a fairy-like great beauty here, can't I ask for her hand?"

The guests in the hall were dumbstruck. These Xie brothers, one publicly protecting a noodle-seller to humiliate his fiancée, the other openly flirting in broad daylight... Have they gone mad?

The Empress rubbed her temples: "Someone, escort Miss Wen back to her residence to rest. As for the two young masters of the Xie family... Another day, this palace will have a proper chat with your father!"

Qionghua walked away without looking back. Behind her came Xie Linyuan's carefree laughter and Xie Linfeng's suppressed, angry reprimand. She suddenly felt that calling off this engagement might be even more troublesome than she had imagined...

Inside the carriage returning to the estate, Qionghua closed her eyes to rest, the wound on the side of her neck aching faintly. Liuying and Pitao didn't dare to breathe loudly, terrified of provoking their mistress's bad mood.

"Miss..." Liuying finally couldn't help herself. "Eldest Young Master Xie, he..."

"Pay him no mind," Qionghua said indifferently. "Just a playboy, that's all."

Yet deep down she knew clearly that Xie Linyuan was by no means as simple as he appeared on the surface. That day in the carriage, his reaction when dodging the arrow had been shockingly fast; today at the princess's estate, the timing of his appearance had been far too coincidental...

Just as she was pondering, the carriage came to an abrupt halt. Outside came the driver's shouts and the sounds of a fight.

Qionghua's eyes snapped open, her hand already resting on the dagger hidden beneath her seat; one she had specially stashed after being ambushed that night.

The carriage curtain was lifted, but what appeared was not the anticipated assassin, but a familiar, bewitching face.

Xie Linyuan leaned lazily against the carriage window, smiling: "Miss Wen, can I catch a free ride?"

Wen Qionghua: "..."

chapters.title: Is She Playing Hard to Get?
chapters.content:
"No," Wen Qionghua said indifferently. "A-Fei, drive on!"

Hearing this, the driver A-Fei immediately cracked his whip and urged the horses forward.

Xie Linyuan, however, gave a playful smile. With a flash, he directly leaped onto the carriage, seating himself steadily on the driver's box, and casually patted A-Fei's shoulder: "Brother, don't be nervous. I'm just hitching a ride."

How could A-Fei dare to disobey? He could only look with a bitter face toward Qionghua inside the carriage compartment.

Qionghua took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the inexplicable irritation surging in her heart: "Eldest Young Master Xie, what is the meaning of this?"

Xie Linyuan lifted a corner of the carriage curtain, that bewitching face appearing exceptionally bewitching in the dim interior: "No particular meaning. Didn't I say? Just hitching a ride."

Xie Linyuan blinked. "Miss Wen isn't unaware that my carriage broke down..."

"..."

Qionghua closed her eyes, finally driven beyond endurance: "Xie Linyuan!"

"Present~" he responded cheerfully.

"You..." Just as she was about to flare up, she suddenly began to cough violently, her complexion turning instantly as pale as paper.

Xie Linyuan's expression changed. He swiftly pulled a porcelain bottle from his chest: "Loquat dew, for stopping coughs."

Qionghua looked at him vigilantly and did not take it.

Xie Linyuan sighed, tasting a drop himself first: "It's not poisonous."

Only then did Qionghua take it and sip a tiny bit. The cool sweetness instantly soothed the itch in her throat, and she paused slightly; this flavor was actually more fitting than the one prescribed by the imperial physicians.

"How is it?" Xie Linyuan tilted his head to look at her, his eyes carrying a hint of expectation.

Qionghua handed the porcelain bottle back to him and said indifferently, "Many thanks. But Eldest Young Master Xie should please return. Between you and me, there is nothing to discuss."

Xie Linyuan wasn't annoyed either; he just smiled meaningfully: "It was specially made for Miss Wen. Just accept it."

She took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the urge to kick him out of the carriage: "Xie Linyuan, please get out."

Seeing that she was truly angry, Xie Linyuan raised his hands in surrender: "Fine, fine, fine, I'm going, I'm going." He made a show of getting down, but then suddenly turned back: "Oh right, Miss Wen..."

"Hn?"

"Your hairpin is crooked."

"......Scram!"

Xie Linyuan leaped off the carriage with a loud laugh, his figure quickly vanishing into the night.

Qionghua trembled with anger at the fingertips, taking quite a while to calm herself down. She rarely experienced such intense emotional fluctuations, yet every time she ran into this person... She subconsciously reached up to touch her hairpin; indeed, it was crooked at a sharp angle from goodness knows when.

"This scoundrel..." she muttered a low curse, though for some reason, the stifled feeling in her chest dissipated quite a bit.

---

On the other side, Xie Linfeng personally escorted Liu Sanniang back to her noodle shop.

Liu Sanniang bit her lip and said softly, "Young Master Xie, today's events... were all because of me. I cannot implicate you any further."

Xie Linfeng furrowed his brow: "It has nothing to do with you; Su Wanrou deliberately stirred up trouble."

Liu Sanniang shook her head, tears in her eyes: "Yet if not for me... Young Master Xie wouldn't have fallen out like this with Miss Wen."

Xie Linfeng felt a tightness in his chest. Remembering the indifferent gaze with which Wen Qionghua had left, his chest felt inexplicably stuffed. He said coldly, "You needn't blame yourself. You and I were never..." He paused, ultimately failing to finish.

Liu Sanniang lifted her eyes to look at him, her gaze full of stubbornness: "Young Master Xie, I am going to the embroidery workshop in the south of the city tomorrow. The silver I owe you, I will slowly pay back."

Hearing this, a surge of irritation abruptly rose in Xie Linfeng's heart: "I won't allow it!" He blurted it out almost instinctively, his tone carrying a domineering edge he hadn't even realized.

Looking at this stubborn yet fragile woman before him, an inexplicable anger mingled with an unclear vexation churned within his chest.

Wen Qionghua calling off the engagement in public had caused him to lose all face, and now even this humble merchant girl, whom he thought he could control and who depended on him, wanted to break free of his control?

Liu Sanniang raised her head; her eye rims were still red, yet her gaze was unusually calm: "Young Master, Sanniang is an orphan girl, and to be favored by the Young Master is already great fortune. But Sanniang cannot live under the Young Master's protection for a lifetime, nor can she... allow the Young Master to be troubled because of me." Her voice trembled slightly, carrying a clarity bordering on despair, "Today's events, Young Master saw them too. Sanniang's existence will only bring shame upon the Young Master, and cause Miss Wen to... grieve."

"What is there for her to grieve over!" Xie Linfeng reacted as if his tail had been stepped on, his voice suddenly rising. "She, Wen Qionghua, is high and mighty; how could she care about a noodle-selling girl like you? Her actions today were merely a posture put on for everyone to see, a slap to my face!"

Liu Sanniang was startled.

Xie Linfeng froze for a moment himself, then said in a deep voice, "You are a weak woman; how much silver can you earn going to an embroidery workshop? Since this shop has been given to you, just stay here in peace."

Liu Sanniang looked at him, her eyes brimming with tears, yet she stubbornly refused to let them fall.

Xie Linfeng's heart stirred slightly. This complete surrender of hers, resigned to her fate, instead acted like a needle, unexpectedly piercing into a hidden corner of Xie Linfeng's heart. Driven by a sudden, unaccountable impulse, he reached out and gently stroked her cheek: "Sanniang, be obedient."

Liu Sanniang's body shuddered, but she did not dodge away. The two exchanged gazes, the atmosphere turning subtle for a moment.

"Young Master!" The pageboy Xiaomai's voice suddenly came from the mouth of the alley: "The Old Master is calling you back to the estate!"

Xie Linfeng snapped back to his senses, withdrew his hand, and his expression returned to normal: "I know."

He turned to leave, but then paused, turning back to say to Liu Sanniang, "Tomorrow... I will come again."

Liu Sanniang kept her head lowered and softly murmured an "mn."

Once Xie Linfeng had walked far away, she slowly raised her head, gazing at his retreating back with complex emotions in her eyes.

Xie Linfeng walked in silence all the way, his face gloomy. His personal pageboy, Xiaomai, cautiously sized up his expression and probed, "Young Master, you don't need to worry about Miss Liu; she won't leave."

Xie Linfeng frowned: "Hm?"

Xiaomai lowered his voice, carrying a bit of the shrewdness of a marketplace local: "Just think about it, she says with her mouth that she's going to the embroidery shop in the south city, but didn't you see? All those dough-kneading utensils in her shop are still sitting right there, and even the dough for tomorrow morning is already kneaded, left to rise under a basin! Does that look like someone who's really about to leave?"

Xie Linfeng paused.

Xiaomai chuckled, "Young Master, you haven't been through much, so you don't understand. Women, they're all like this, saying no with their mouths, but who knows how much they're hoping for it in their hearts! My sweetheart, Cuihua, took a fancy to a hairpin at the East Street silverware shop, and every day she muttered to me, saying, 'Oh, it's too expensive, I don't want it at all.' And the result? I gritted my teeth and bought it for her, and she hugged me and jumped up and down with joy! This is called 'playing hard to get'!"

Playing hard to get...

In Xie Linfeng's mind, Wen Qionghua's cold, peerless face, the one that had ultimately left him with only an indifferent back, unexpectedly overlapped with the image of Liu Sanniang lowering her head in tears.

Could it be that Wen Qionghua's decisive words of calling off the engagement today were also... a move of advancing by retreating? Wanting to force him to lower his head, to make him beg her?

This notion was absurd in the extreme, yet like a poisonous vine, it instantly wound itself tightly around his heart. An indescribable, complex emotion surged up; there was the anger of being played for a fool, a faint unwillingness, and a trace of something he himself was unwilling to admit, secret relief.

If that was really the case, then wasn't Wen Qionghua... entirely devoid of feeling for him? Was she merely using this extreme method to express her dissatisfaction and... care?

Xie Linfeng gave a derisive smile, yet the gloom in his heart inexplicably dispersed quite a bit.

He let out a cold hum, no longer looking in the direction of the noodle shop, and instead turned to stride toward the Xie residence, his pace noticeably lighter than when he had come. Xiaomai watched his young master's expression shift from overcast to clear, and assuming he had rendered a great service, followed along with a smug look.

chapters.title: Family Discipline
chapters.content:
The Xie Residence, Pine and Crane Hall.

The atmosphere was as heavy as the dead calm before a storm.

Xie Yun, the old patriarch, sat upright at the top seat, his hair and beard completely white, his face ashen. The sandalwood cane in his hand thumped heavily against the floor tiles, producing a dull, echoing sound.

Below, Xie Linfeng stood with his head bowed. His mother, the mistress of the Xie family, Madam Su, was wiping away tears with a handkerchief.

"Father! You must see the truth! Feng'er is young and vigorous, a bit impulsive perhaps, but that Wen girl went too far! Just a sickly weakling, yet relying on her good family background, she dared to humiliate Feng'er like that in the Princess's Manor, right in front of the Empress! They aren't even married yet, and she's already so arrogant and domineering; what will happen in the future? In my opinion, this marriage might as well be called off! With our Feng'er's looks and character, he'd be a fine match even for a princess!"

Xie Linfeng's grandmother, the elderly matriarch, chimed in from the side as well: "Indeed! That Wen Qionghua looks short-lived and lacking in fortune, the kind of person who blows over in the breeze; how is she supposed to spread branches and scatter leaves for our Xie family? Feng'er was merely protecting a pitiful person, and she? She went right up to the Empress! Isn't this deliberately trying to ruin Feng'er's future?"

Sitting to the side, Xie Changlin, the Prime Minister, furrowed his brow deeply. Several times he wanted to speak, but each time he was stopped dead by his wife Su's glaring eyes.

He wearily rubbed the bridge of his nose, his gaze sweeping over his eldest, concubine-born son, Xie Linyuan, who was standing in the shadows of the corner with a detached expression, even wearing a slight, amused smile as if watching a play.

"And you!" The anger of the old patriarch Xie Yun finally found another outlet. His hawk-like gaze nailed itself viciously onto Xie Linyuan. "You wretched creature! Today at the Princess's Manor, your brother was publicly humiliated, and instead of thinking to uphold the family's dignity, you poured oil on the fire and openly flirted with that Wen Qionghua! You've completely thrown away the Xie family's face!"

Xie Linyuan lazily picked his ear, as if he hadn't heard the deafening roar. Instead, he smiled and said, "Grandfather puts it quite harshly. This grandson is wronged. This grandson merely saw that Miss Wen had suffered a grievance, wanted to comfort her, and incidentally secure a wife for himself. Doesn't Your Old Eminence always scold me for not doing honest work and losing face for the Xie family? Besides, Second Brother doesn't like her anyway; if this grandson can manage to marry the apple of the Xuanhe Prince's Estate's eye, wouldn't that be a monumental achievement?"

"You... you bastard!" Xie Yun trembled all over with rage, grabbed a teacup from the table, and hurled it!

The teacup grazed the corner of Xie Linyuan's forehead and shattered with a bang against a pillar. Linyuan didn't even dodge. A shallow bloody scratch was torn across his temple by a flying shard. He raised a hand to wipe away the drop of blood, looking at the crimson smear on his fingertips. The smile at the corners of his lips deepened, while the depths of his eyes remained a sheet of cold indifference.

"Rebellious son! Rebellious son!" Xie Yun panted heavily with fury. "Men! Bring the family discipline! Beat this shameless wretch who ruins our family morals to death!"

A heavy rattan staff was quickly brought in. Two sturdy servants stepped forward and pinned Xie Linyuan down.

"Father!" Xie Changlin finally couldn't help but speak out.

"Shut up!" Xie Yun barked. "Whoever dares to plead for him today gets beaten as well!"

A trace of malicious satisfaction flashed across the eyes of Madam Su and the elderly matriarch as they looked on coldly.

The rattan staff fell heavily with a whistling sound, striking flesh and bone with a dull thud.

Xie Linyuan was pinned and forced to his knees on the ground, his teeth clenched tightly, not uttering a single sound. His moon-white brocade robe was quickly soaked through with blood, cold sweat poured down his temples, and his demonic face was twisted from the pain, yet a sarcastic curve consistently lingered at the corner of his mouth.

After twenty strikes of the staff, Xie Linyuan was practically dragged out by the servants. Still unsatisfied with his anger, Xie Yun pointed at Xie Changlin: "Look at the good sons you've spawned! One and all, they're here to collect debts!" With that, he flicked his sleeves and stormed off.

---

Xie Linyuan's courtyard was situated in the most remote western corner of the Xie Residence, named "Listening Bamboo Pavilion." The name was refined, yet it exuded desolation. Patches of moss speckled the yard, and a few thin bamboo stalks rustled softly in the night wind, making it feel even more solitary.

A white-haired, kind-faced old woman was already waiting at the door; Nanny Zhao, who had raised Xie Linyuan since childhood.

She could not speak. At this moment, watching Xie Linyuan being half-carried and half-supported back by two pages, along with the startling bloodstains seeping through his back, tears instantly welled up in her cloudy, aged eyes. She gestured frantically, her throat emitting anxious "Ah-ah" sounds.

"Nanny... don't worry..." Xie Linyuan's face was as pale as paper, cold sweat streaming down his temples, yet he forced himself to pull off a reassuring smile, his voice hoarse.

Nanny Zhao's tears fell even harder. She clumsily gestured, signaling him to hurry inside, and pointed to the medicinal herbs and hot water she had prepared.

The two servants carefully helped Xie Linyuan lie face down on the bed and then withdrew. Nanny Zhao immediately stepped forward, took out the pre-prepared medicine, and meticulously applied it to his wounds. Her movements were practiced and gentle; clearly, this was not her first time doing such a thing.

Xie Linyuan closed his eyes, his thick eyelashes casting shadows on his pale face. His teeth were clenched as he endured the sharp pain brought by the medicinal powder irritating his wounds, but his body relaxed, leaving him to the care of this elderly woman who was like a mother to him.

Lying prone on the couch, Xie Linyuan let her tend to him and even joked, "Nanny's skills are getting better and better. Applying this medicine doesn't hurt at all."

Nanny Zhao glared at him and purposefully increased the pressure of her hand.

"Ouch!" Xie Linyuan exaggeratedly cried out. "Nanny, are you trying to murder your own son?"

Nanny Zhao was amused by him and gestured a few times more, meaning to scold him for not knowing how to look after himself.

Xie Linyuan couldn't help but draw a breath, his body moving unconsciously, and his elbow accidentally bumped against the medicine bowl sitting on the small tea table beside the bed.

Just as the bowl filled with brownish medicinal broth was about to crash to the floor, a wrinkled yet extraordinarily steady hand flashed out like lightning and caught the bowl securely, not a single drop of the broth spilling!

The movement was so fast it left only an afterimage; definitely not something an ordinary old woman could achieve!

Yet Xie Linyuan acted as if he were completely accustomed to it. He merely lazily lifted his eyelids to glance at it, then laid his head back down.

Nanny Zhao reproachfully glared at him, gesturing for him to behave and drink his medicine quickly.

She handed the medicine bowl to Xie Linyuan's lips, watching him frown and gulp it down, before a look of mingled heartache and helplessness finally appeared on her face.

She gently patted his back and pointed outside, signaling him to rest well while she stood guard outside.

Nanny Zhao was the one who had followed Xie Changlin and an infant Xie Linyuan back to the Xie Residence all those years ago.

She had been the personal maid of Xie Linyuan's biological mother. Because she was born mute and illiterate, no matter how the Xie family probed, cajoled, or threatened, they could never extract a single shred of information about Xie Linyuan's birth mother from her.

Over time, the Xie family gave up, simply treating her as an insignificant old servant by Xie Linyuan's side.

Carrying the empty medicine bowl, Nanny Zhao light-footedly retreated and carefully pulled the door shut.

Inside the room, Xie Linyuan was left alone. The pain and vulnerability on his face vanished without a trace, replaced by a cold, dead calm.

Candlelight flickered in the bottomless depths of his pupils, reflecting a hint of sharpness and exhaustion.

"Come out," he spoke in a low voice to the empty, quiet room.

A dark shadow appeared silently beside the bed like a ghost, dropping to one knee.

"Master," Moying's voice was low and wave-less. "The matter has been handled properly. However... should we keep an eye on Miss Wen's side?"

Xie Linyuan closed his eyes and gave a soft "Mn."

Hearing the words "Miss Wen," Xie Linyuan's tightly shut eyelashes trembled imperceptibly.

After a moment of silence.

"No need." Xie Linyuan slowly opened his eyes. The strange, seductive peach-blossom eyes no longer held a shred of playfulness, leaving only the dark gloom of a deep pool and an almost paranoid focus.

A faint, heart-stopping curve touched the corners of his lips, his voice as light as the night wind brushing past bamboo leaves:

"I'll do it myself."

chapters.title: Paying a Visit
chapters.content:
When Wen Qionghua returned to the estate, the household was already in an uproar. Her three brothers swarmed around her aggressively.

"That scoundrel Xie Linfeng! How dare he bully my sister like this!" Second Brother Wen Rui kicked over a rosewood low table in the hall, his fists cracking as he clenched them. "I'll take men to the Xie residence right now and break that bastard's legs!" As a military officer on duty, he immediately grabbed his saber and prepared to leave.

Third Brother Wen Yu (Wen Yu), the youngest who had just returned from school, was already charging out with a riding whip: "Tie him up? That's letting him off too light! Break his legs straight away so he won't dare bully my sister ever again!"

Eldest Brother Wen Jing, who served in the Dali Temple, usually a refined and scholarly official, currently wore a similarly gloomy expression. The folding fan in his hand was already being crushed to creaks: "I'm going with you."

"All of you, stop." Wen Qionghua's voice was very soft, yet it made her three brothers instantly freeze in their tracks.

Her face was pale, with faint dark circles under her eyes, clearly showing she was utterly exhausted. She raised her eyes to sweep over her three elder brothers and said lightly, "I'm tired. I want to rest."

Wen Jing looked at his sister with heartache: "Qionghua, we can't let this matter rest like this!"

"I know," Qionghua smiled faintly. "But what good does beating him up do? The engagement is still there, the dignity of both families is still there. Making a huge fuss will only let outsiders make a joke of us."

Qionghua wearily rubbed the bridge of her nose, her voice fatigued: "Brothers, I'm tired."

Her words instantly quieted her three furious brothers.

"Qionghua..." Seeing her pale face and the faint bruises under her eyes, her brothers felt a pang of deep distress. Ultimately suppressing their anger, they muttered, "Alright, you rest first. We'll talk about this later," and carefully escorted her back to her room.

However, she had barely lain down for long when the doorman hurried in to report: "Miss, there is a lady surnamed Liu outside asking to see you."

Liuying and Bitao exchanged glances. Bitao couldn't help blurting out, "Liu Sanniang? How does she still dare to come?"

Qionghua closed her eyes, her brows furrowed slightly. If she saw her, it would stick in her throat; if she didn't, people would accuse her of being arrogant later on.

Liuying lowered her voice: "If Miss doesn't want to see her, this maid will go send her away."

Qionghua was silent for a moment before finally shaking her head: "Just say I'm ill and inconvenient to receive guests." She paused. "Send her back in a carriage."

Liuying acknowledged the order and left.

Standing alone by the window, looking at the falling begonia petals in the courtyard, Qionghua suddenly felt overwhelmingly tired. It wasn't that she held no resentment, she simply couldn't be bothered with the entanglement. Whether it was Xie Linfeng or Liu Sanniang, Wen Qionghua's life should not be wasted on such meaningless squabbles.

Outside the Wen gates, Liu Sanniang twisted her handkerchief in her hands. She herself didn't know why she had turned her steps toward the Wen Residence; she wanted to apologize to Wen Qionghua; not just for what happened during the day, but also for just now...

Although she knew the gap in their social standing and was prepared to leave, deep down... how could her heart not flutter for someone so orchid-like and jade-pure, yet so caring and helpful toward her?

Though she came to apologize, a secret expectation still blossomed in her heart.

"My miss is feeling unwell and is inconvenient to receive guests. Fearing you might encounter trouble on the road, she specifically ordered this maid to send you back." Liuying's voice was cold yet adhered to proper etiquette.

"Then I won't disturb the noble family; I can go back by myself." For some reason, she actually felt a sense of relief.

"Miss Liu, hold on. My miss asked me to bring you a word; the path was chosen by yourself, don't regret it." Without waiting for Liu Sanniang to react, Liuying turned and left. Our miss is kind-hearted and doesn't care, even wanting to send Liu Sanniang back, but since she said she didn't want it herself, so be it, she thought, hurrying back to serve her miss.

---

Early the next morning, Old Patriarch Xie personally brought Xie Linfeng over to offer an apology. Though the elderly matriarch and Madam Su were unwilling, they had no choice but to tag along.

After all, the two families' marriage was bestowed by the late emperor; if it truly reached the point of a broken engagement, it would be a severe blow to the Xie family's reputation.

Yet, was there half an ounce of apology on the faces of this mother-in-law and daughter-in-law? The elderly matriarch wore a rigid expression, looking precisely as though someone owed her eight hundred taels of silver; Madam Su forced a smile, but it was so fake it couldn't fool a three-year-old child. Even Xie Linfeng wore a gloomy face.

The Wen family members greeted them with cold expressions, the atmosphere so heavy it could wring out water.

"Today, this old man has come specifically to bring this wretch to make amends," Xie Yun cupped his fists, his tone sincere.

Prince Wen formally returned the courtesy.

"Where is Miss Wen?" Madam Su glanced around, feigning concern. "Is she perhaps feeling unwell?"

Wen Madam Xiao said coldly, "Qionghua suffered a fright last night, and her old ailment flared up again. She can't get out of bed."

The elderly matriarch furrowed her brows, clearly displeased: "We came to visit in person, and she won't even show her face? Is this the Wen family's etiquette?"

Madam Su was even more snide: "We understand that Qionghua has a frail constitution. But her future mother-in-law has come and she won't even see her; what will happen after she enters the Xie household?" She smiled pointedly, "Though it doesn't matter much. If Linfeng truly takes in someone else later, she can share the burden for her."

"Madam Su!" Eldest Brother Wen Jing tightly closed his folding fan with a snap. "What do you mean by that?!"

"What do I mean?" Madam Su feigned surprise. "Aren't three wives and four concubines a common thing for men? Furthermore, Linfeng is destined to inherit the Xie family's title in the future; spreading branches and scattering leaves is his responsibility. Since Qionghua has a weak constitution, having someone share the burden for her is also for her own good."

Bang! Second Brother Wen Rui abruptly slammed the table and stood up. "My Wen family has no such thing as taking concubines!"

Madam Su feigned surprise: "Second Young Master Wen, don't misunderstand. I'm doing this for Qionghua's sake too. Her health is weak; someone needs to help manage the household chores, don't they? Linfeng was merely pitying that orphan girl, yet Miss Wen made a mountain out of a molehill and kicked up a fuss all the way to the Empress. Her temper is really a bit too fierce."

Third Brother Wen Yu sneered: "Madam Xie has a thick skin! My sister isn't even married into your family yet, and you're already scheming to stuff people into your son's chambers?"

Xie Linfeng stood to the side, his complexion extremely ugly. He had come today to apologize, but these words from his mother were undoubtedly pouring oil on the fire.

Unflustered, Madam Su continued her insinuation: "Breaking off the marriage would be bad for both families. Besides..." She swept a meaningful glance over the Wen family members present, "The engagement between Qionghua and Linfeng is known throughout the capital. If it's truly called off, aside from the Xie family, I'm afraid no one else would dare marry her."

As soon as these words fell, the hall erupted in uproar. The Wen brothers turned ashen with anger, and even the usually steady Wen Jing clenched his fists.

"What a bold statement; 'no one else would dare marry her'!"

An authoritative, aged voice suddenly came from outside the door.

Everyone turned their head to see an elderly man with white hair and beard, full of vigor and vitality, striding in. It was none other than the newly returned Old Prince Xuanhe!

"Grandfather!" Wen Jing and the others hurriedly stood up to salute.

The Old Prince let out a cold snort, his gaze sweeping across Madam Su like a sharp blade: "If this old man hadn't returned, I'm afraid the apple of my family's eye would have been bullied to death by the likes of you!"

chapters.title: Where Did This Brother-in-Law Come From?
chapters.content:
Everyone turned around and saw an elderly man with white hair striding in. Still in his military uniform, he looked travel-worn yet imposing; it was none other than the recently returned Prince Xuanhe, Wen Jing.

"Father!" "Grandfather!" cried the members of the Wen family in pleasant surprise.

The Old Prince let out a cold snort. "You all have so little backbone. If this old man hadn't returned, who knows how much more grievance my darling girl would have suffered!" With that, without even glancing at the Xie family, he walked straight to the head seat.

Madam Su's face turned pale, and she hurriedly stood up to bow. "You flatter us, Old Prince. This concubine has no such intention..."

"Shut up!" The Old Prince waved a hand, cutting her off completely without giving her an ounce of face, and turned instead to Old Master Xie. "Old Man Xie, is this the sincerity of your Xie family? Bringing such trash to run wild in my Wen estate?"

The Dowager didn't even dare to speak. The juniors hadn't seen it, but she had personally witnessed this fierce god's "heroic deeds" of hanging a few heads from his waist back in the day.

Old Master Xie wore an awkward expression on his face and hurriedly stood up to cup his fists in salute. "Old Prince, please calm your anger! This matter is due to the Xie family's lax discipline, but the marriage engagement was bestowed by the late Emperor, so it must not be broken! Our Xie family will never let Qionghua suffer even the slightest grievance!"

Prince Xuanhe raised a hand to interrupt. "Old Man Xie, you and I have been friends for many years, so let's dispense with the polite pleasantries."

He lightly tapped the tabletop, his voice resonant and leaving no room for argument! "Today, let's lay our cards on the table; this marriage might as well not happen at all! In my Wen family, there has never been any such thing as taking concubines!"

The Wen family had many sons, but Old Prince Wen and his late wife shared a deep and devoted bond. After the Old Princess passed away, the Old Prince never once thought of remarrying. The family tradition was upright and righteous. From the Old Prince down to Wen Qionghua's various brothers, every single one of them practiced lifelong monogamy.

At this moment, the main hall fell silent.

Old Master Xie said anxiously, "Brother Wen, this matter still needs to be discussed thoroughly! After all, it was a marriage bestowed by the late Emperor..."

"The late Emperor bestowed the marriage because he valued the matching social standing of our two families and the compatibility of our children," Prince Xuanhe said coldly. "But now Second Young Master Xie has someone else in his heart. If my granddaughter marries over there, wouldn't she be living like a widow? What use is keeping a marriage engagement like this?"

Xie Linfeng abruptly raised his head, a flash of panic crossing his eyes. "I didn't..." Then, remembering something, his voice lowered to a mosquito's buzz.

Madam Su couldn't help chiming in, "My Lord, you can't put it that way. Linfeng is young, and it's inevitable that he was led astray by some seductive hussies, but the position of primary wife will always be Miss Wen's..."

"Shut up!" Prince Xuanhe's sharp shout made Madam Su jump. "The daughters of the Wen family will never play second fiddle to anyone!"

He turned to Old Master Xie, his tone softening slightly. "Old Man Xie, let me ask you this today, if it were your own daughter being treated with such contempt, what would you do?"

Old Master Xie was left speechless.

Prince Xuanhe let out a long sigh. "Since that's the case, let's break off this engagement. I will personally submit a memorial to the Emperor to state the reasons clearly. This old man will shoulder all the blame."

The Xie family members were thrown into panic. The Emperor valued the reputation of aristocratic families above all else. If this matter were brought before the Emperor, the consequences would be unimaginable!

"Grandfather!" A weak yet clear voice suddenly came from outside the hall.

Everyone turned around to see Wen Qionghua in plain clothes, slowly walking in with Liuying's support. Her face was as pale as paper, with almost no color on her lips, save for her eyes, which were startlingly clear.

"Darling! Why did you get up?" Wen Jing hurriedly stood up.

Qionghua bowed to her grandfather, looking at the old man, who had clearly made an expedited journey back, with tears shimmering in her eyes. "Grandfather, your granddaughter is unfilial and has caused you worry." This instantly broke the Old Prince's heart.

Only then did Wen Qionghua look at the Xie family. "Calling off the engagement is Qionghua's willful decision; I should not let Grandfather bear the burden." She turned to Old Master Xie and made a deep bow. "Grandfather Xie, the fault here lies neither with the Xie family nor the Wen family; it is simply that Qionghua and Second Young Master Xie are not meant to be. Qionghua is willing to personally submit the memorial to annul the engagement."

Xie Linfeng stared fixedly at her, his chest heaving violently. "Wen Qionghua, you..."

"Second Young Master Xie." Qionghua looked at him calmly, without a single ripple in her eyes. "I've said it before: between you and me, there was never any bond to begin with."

Xie Linfeng's heart was shaken. He couldn't understand it; he had already swallowed his pride to come and apologize, what more did she want from him?

Perhaps it was because he had spent too much time in temples, growing used to all sorts of pilgrims praying for things they couldn't have; or perhaps because he had known since childhood that he had a predestined fiancée. Therefore, no matter how beautiful Wen Qionghua was, he had always felt she was like a screen in his bedchamber, or an ink seal on his desk, destined to remain right there forever...

Old Master Xie looked at Qionghua, then looked at his own grandson. No, this won't do! Absolutely cannot break off this engagement! Although his son was already a prestigious Chancellor, their foundation at court could not possibly compare to the Wen family's merits of helping establish the dynasty. Over the years, it was precisely by relying on the marriage alliance with the Prince's Estate that no one dared to criticize their actions in court.
