Once this marriage was annulled, let alone being cast aside by the Emperor, even though the Xuanhe Prince's Estate consisted of military generals, they had countless loyal retainers and followers. In the future at court... He didn't dare to imagine the future.

Just as he was about to speak, before a single word left his mouth, the doorman suddenly ran in hurriedly and deliberately reported in a loud voice,

"My Lord! Just now, a servant from the Xie family came to report that several ruffians surrounded the entrance of the Xie residence, claiming to be the two brothers-in-law of Second Young Master Xie! They allegedly owe hundreds of silver taels at a gambling den and are demanding that the Xie family pay to redeem them, threatening to report to the officials if the Xie family doesn't cough up the money! They even said..."

The doorman deliberately paused, his voice growing even louder. "They also said that although the Xie family is a prominent and noble household, paying one's debts is only natural, and they shouldn't even think about defaulting!"

The doorman added, "That group of scoundrels said the two brothers-in-law's surname is Liu, and they've already headed to the noodle shop bought by Second Young Master Xie!"

Hearing this, Xie Linfeng's expression changed drastically, and he abruptly stood up. "San Niang!"

Disregarding all propriety, he turned and sprinted outside.

"You wretch! Stop right there!" Old Master Xie roared angrily.

Yet Xie Linfeng turned a deaf ear, disappearing outside in the blink of an eye.

The Old Prince cast a meaningful look at his three sons, then turned back to Old Master Xie. "Old Man Xie, which branch of the family tree did your grandson recognize these 'brothers-in-law' from?"

The eldest brother, Wen Jing, immediately waved his hands. "I certainly don't have a gambling habit!"

The second brother, Wen Rui, shook his head right away. "My surname is Wen, not Liu!"

The third brother, Wen Yu, rolled his eyes. "I am definitely not Second Young Master Xie's brother-in-law!"

Old Master Xie was trembling with rage, while the Dowager and Madam Su turned deathly pale.

The Old Prince looked coldly at Old Master Xie and slowly said, "Brother Xie, are these your Xie family's fine young men?"

Old Master Xie's face turned ashen, and he slumped defeatedly back into his chair.

As for Wen Qionghua, from beginning to end, she never spared him another glance.

At that moment, no one noticed that outside the Wen residence, inside a carriage, a flash of red lazily leaned back, fingers toying with a medicine bottle while the corners of the lips hooked into an amused smile.

chapters.title: Everyone Loves Gossip
chapters.content:
Liu Sanniang curled up in the corner of the noodle shop, un-dried tear tracks still staining her face. Outside the door, Liu Da and Liu Er, along with four or five gambling den thugs, were violently pounding on the door.

"Bitch! Get your ass out here!" Liu Da kicked the door panel, causing the porcelain bowls on the cupboard to rattle loudly. "You think you can hide and be fine?"

"Little sister," Liu Er chimed in with hypocritical persuasion, "your brothers have no choice. We owe the Hongyun Gambling Den five hundred silver taels. If we don't pay up, they really are going to chop off our hands!"

Inside the door, Liu Sanniang bit her lip hard and stayed silent.

"My ass! Liu Da, Liu Er, you two bastards aren't trying to scam me, are you?" Lin Ran, the manager of the gambling den, dressed in a green scholar's robe, strolled in leisurely while twirling a sharp dagger in his hand.

"You two keep insisting that your sister is Second Young Master Xie's woman. We went to the Xie residence to demand money earlier and got chased right back out. Offending an official's household like this; do you two have enough pairs of hands for me to chop off?" Linran exuded a ruffian aura that clashed completely with his scholarly face.

"This little one... this little one speaks the absolute truth! Look at this shop, Second Young Master Xie gave it to my sister!" Liu Da fawned while banging on the door.

"That's right, Manager Lin! What my brother said is true. Come inside and take a look at the shop. Once she hands over the property deed, there are valuable things in here. If all else fails, take a look at my sister here; she caught Second Young Master Xie's eye, so she's got good looks and can fetch an even higher price to offset the debt!" Liu Er pounded on the door even more eagerly.

Crash! The door bolt finally snapped.

"Wretched girl! Where did you hide the property deed?!" Liu Da grabbed Liu Sanniang by the hair, fiercely pressing her for an answer.

"Big brother... this shop isn't mine... Young Master Xie just lent it to me..." Liu Sanniang wept from the pain, yet she bit her lip so hard she refused to let go.

"Bullsit!" Liu Er kicked over the cutting board, sending bowls and dishes shattering across the floor. "Second Young Master Xie treats you so well, didn't he just give you this shop as a gift? Stop talking nonsense! Hand over the property deed right now! The men from Hongyun Gambling Den are waiting!"

Liu Sanniang shook her head in despair. "No... I can't... I really don't have a property deed... and I can't give you this shop either..."

Liu Da grabbed Liu Sanniang by the hair and dragged her outward. "Fine! Let's go! We're going to the Xie residence right now to demand money! Doesn't Second Young Master Xie dote on you? Five hundred taels is nothing to him!"

"Little sister, you can't just sit by and let us die!" Liu Er hypocritically persuaded, his eyes greedily scanning the shop. "Second Young Master Xie dotes on you so much; just bat your eyelashes and throw a tantrum at him; what's a little silver to someone like him?"

"I'm not going!" Liu Sanniang suddenly screamed and struggled. "I'll pay off the shop's cost slowly, but I will no longer drag Young Master Xie into this!"

Linran frowned, signaling Liu Da to let go of her first. "Miss Liu, your two brothers owe us five hundred taels. This shop is in a decent location, so taking it as collateral happens to work out just fine. If you know what's good for you, obediently sign and press your thumbprint, and it'll save us..." He cast a meaningful glance at Liu Da and Liu Er, "...damaging the family harmony."

Elsewhere, Xie Linfeng rode his horse at a gallop, burning with anxiety. He should have guessed long ago that those two scoundrel brothers of the Liu family would stir up trouble! Sanniang was so delicate, how could she withstand their coercion?

"Young Master! Wait for me!" The pageboy Xiaomai panted as he chased after him.

Rounding a street corner, a troop of riders suddenly appeared ahead. Leading them was a man in red lazily leaning against his horse's back, a folding fan swaying in his hand; it was none other than Xie Linyuan.

"Yo, where is Second Brother rushing off to?" Xie Linyuan smilingly blocked his path.

"Get out of the way!" Xie Linfeng shouted coldly.

Xie Linyuan didn't budge an inch, instead leaning in closer. "Grandfather is at the Wen residence making amends, yet you run off for a noodle-selling woman... Tsk tsk, Second Brother, are you determined to drag the Xie family's reputation through the mud before you're satisfied?"

Xie Linfeng tightened his grip on the reins. "My affairs require no interference from Big Brother!"

"How can I not interfere?" Xie Linyuan's smile grew wider. "You publicly humiliated Miss Wen, causing the Xie family to be pointed at and berated by the Old Prince. And now you abandon family dignity for a mere woman... Second Brother, your sense of responsibility as the 'future head of the Xie family' is truly an eye-opener."

Xie Linfeng's face turned livid, and he abruptly lashed his horse forward, shouting, "Get lost!"

Xie Linyuan sidestepped to avoid him, watching his receding figure with a hint of mockery in his eyes. He turned and made a hand gesture toward the shadows, whereupon a group of stout gossips quietly followed behind.

---

Liu Sanniang shook her head in despair. "This shop isn't mine... Young Master Xie lent it to me so I could have a place to settle down and make a living. I can't..."

Slap! A vicious backhand landed hard across her face.

"Shameless wretch!" Liu Da's face was ferocious. "Do you really think you're the young mistress of the Xie family? Second Young Master Xie was just playing around with you! We went to the Xie residence, and he didn't even show his face! It got us another beating for nothing! You useless, good-for-nothing hussy!"

Blood seeped from the corner of Liu Sanniang's mouth, and her vision darkened. She gripped her clothes tightly, her fingernails digging into her palms. Her heart was filled with absolute despair.

Suddenly, the shop door was kicked open with a bang!

"Sanniang!"

Xie Linfeng stood against the light at the entrance, his moon-white brocade robe fluttering in the wind. His gaze swept over the messy wreckage and finally landed on Liu Sanniang's swollen, bruised face, his pupils violently contracting.

"S-Second Young Master Xie?" Liu Da let go in fright, retreating step by step.

Xie Linfeng strode forward, pulling Liu Sanniang behind him, his voice as cold as ice. "Have you grown tired of living?"

Liu Er's legs went weak, and he dropped to his knees. "Spare my life, Young Master Xie! We were just... just coming to borrow a little silver from our sister..."

"Borrow?" Xie Linfeng sneered, lifting his foot to kick a nearby bench into splinters. "Smashing up a shop and beating people; you call that borrowing?"

Liu Da suddenly stuck out his neck and yelled, "Since Second Young Master Xie has taken a fancy to my sister, then we're family! What's wrong with family helping each other out? We owe money at the gambling den; shouldn't you help us pay it back?"

"Shut up!" Liu Sanniang suddenly shrieked. "Do you two have any shame left?!"

Xie Linfeng took a deep breath, suppressing his surging anger, and turned to the gambling den manager. "How much do they owe?"

Linran held up five fingers. "Five hundred taels."

Xie Linfeng sneered, pulled a bank note from his chest pocket, and slapped it onto the table. "Get lost."

The manager picked up the note, looked at it, and suddenly smiled. "Second Young Master Xie, this money... I'm afraid it's not enough."

"What do you mean?"

"With compound interest, it's a thousand taels now," Linran said leisurely. "And..." He cast a meaningful glance at Liu Sanniang. "Our boss said that if you can't pay it back, Miss Liu coming to the Drunken Immortal Pavilion to play the lute and sing for a few days will also do."

"Audacious!" Xie Linfeng erupted in fury, whipping out the sword at his waist and pressing it against Linran's throat. "Just try touching her!"

Linran remained unfazed. "Second Young Master Xie, you're an elite scholar of the Hanlin Academy. Committing murder in broad daylight... wouldn't look too good, would it?"

Xie Linfeng's sword-wielding hand trembled slightly as reason and rage fought a fierce battle in his mind.

At that moment, several sharp voices drifted in from outside:

"Aiyo, what a fine scene of a hero saving a beauty."

"Let me see, let me see, isn't this the Second Young Master of Chancellor Xie's household?"

"Aiyo, well I never, it really is! Isn't he engaged to that young lady from the Prince's Estate?"

"Forget it! Look at this pair of lovebirds, how affectionate they are!"

"Second Young Master Xie is truly deeply devoted to the Liu family's girl!"

...

A large group of stout aunties appeared from nowhere, packing the entrance of the noodle shop so tightly not even water could get through.

Anyone who paid attention to gossip would recognize this bunch of aunties, commonly known as the capital's super megaphones. Through their mouths, there was no gossip in the world that couldn't be broadcasted...

chapters.title: Boiling Rumors
chapters.content:
Xie Linfeng's hand holding the sword trembled slightly. In his ears were the sharp and shrill discussions of the plump matrons, and before his eyes was Lin Ran's smile-that-wasn't-a-smile. He suddenly felt as though he had seen this person somewhere before.

"Second Young Master Xie, look at how this has turned out..." Lin Ran spread his hands in a feigned display of helplessness. "How about this, why don't you put down the sword first, and we can talk this over properly?"

Sanniang suddenly lunged forward, grabbing Xie Linfeng's arm in a death grip: "Young Master Xie! Don't be rash!"

With this embrace, the gossiping aunties at the doorway instantly blew up:

"Oh my goodness! Hugging and embracing in broad daylight!"

"Tsk tsk tsk, Second Young Master Xie is quite the lucky dog!"

"I heard that Miss Wen is still sick in bed, yet here he is, being all lovey-dovey with the Liu girl..."

Xie Linfeng's face turned livid, but he had no choice but to sheath his sword. He swept his cold gaze across the crowd: "If anyone dares to spread nonsense about today's events..."

"Oh my! Is Second Young Master Xie trying to threaten us common folk?"

A matron dressed in loud reds and greens shrilly interrupted. "Did everyone hear that? The Second Young Master of the Xie family wants to seal our mouths!"

"Exactly, exactly!" others immediately chimed in, "We all saw it with our own eyes!"

Xie Linfeng's temples throbbed violently.

He knew that whatever happened today, there was no hiding it anymore. The mouths of these long-tongued gossips were even more capable of twisting right and wrong than the censors in the imperial court.

"Manager Lin," he forced down his anger, "One thousand liang, right? I didn't bring that much cash with me; tomorrow I'll send someone to the gambling house."

Lin Ran, however, shook his head: "Second Young Master Xie, our boss said we want cash now."

"You..."

"Young Master Xie!" Sanniang suddenly dropped to her knees. "This humble girl isn't worth you going through this! I'll find a way to pay back this money, I beg you, don't..."

"Stop talking!" Xie Linfeng hauled her up by the arm, his voice dropping to a harsh whisper, "Are you still trying to make things chaotic enough?"

Sanniang trembled from his roar, tears falling like pattering rain.

This scene prompted yet another round of pointing and whispering from the aunties.

"What a sin, scaring that poor girl to tears..."

"I heard those two older brothers of the Liu girl are good for nothing, coming every day to demand money..."

"If you ask me, since Second Young Master Xie fancies her, he should marry her properly! What is this unclear, messy business right now?"

Veins bulged on Xie Linfeng's forehead, and just as he was about to erupt, he heard a commotion drift over from the head of the street.

"Make way! Everyone make way!"

A team of servants dressed in Xie family livery parted the crowd, led by Xiaomai, Xie Linfeng's personal valet. He squeezed through sweating profusely, whispering into Xie Linfeng's ear: "Young Master! The Grand Patriarch has spoken, telling you to return to the manor immediately! The Wen family... the Wen family wants to call off the engagement!"

Xie Linfeng's whole body gave a violent start: "What?"

"The Old Prince has taken Miss Wen into the palace to see the Emperor! The Grand Patriarch was so angry he passed out! The Mistress told you to hurry back!"

It was as if Xie Linfeng had been struck by lightning; for a moment, he didn't even know how to react.

Seeing this, Lin Ran piped up with a sarcastic tone: "Looks like Second Young Master Xie has matters at home? Then this one thousand liang..."

"Give it to him," a languid voice drifted from outside the crowd.

Everyone looked back and saw Xie Linyuan leisurely strolling over, his vermilion robes catching the eye particularly sharply in the sunlight. He casually tossed a heavy brocade pouch to Lin Ran: "Count it. Only more, not less."

Lin Ran caught the money bag, his expression shifting slightly before cupping his fists: "First Young Master Xie is most straightforward! Let's go!" With that, he led the gamblers away in a swift retreat.

Liu Da and Liu Er also tried to slip away, but Xie Linyuan kicked them to the ground one by one: "What's the rush? Aren't you girls' 'good brothers'? Shouldn't you stay behind to clean up the mess?"

Only then did Xie Linfeng snap back to his senses, casting a complicated look at Xie Linyuan: "Xie Linyuan..."

"Don't," Xie Linyuan waved a hand. "I'm not here to help you." He leaned in close, speaking in a voice only the two of them could hear, "I'm just here to watch the show~"

Xie Linfeng's pupils constricted.

Xie Linyuan straightened up, patted his shoulder, his voice returning to its usual flippancy: "Second brother, Grandfather has fainted, Father is furious, the Wen family wants to call off the wedding... and you still have the leisure to play the hero saving the damsel here? Tsk tsk, such deep and loyal affection~"

As soon as these words left his mouth, the surrounding aunties exploded once more:

"Good heavens! The Wen family is really calling off the wedding?"

"You bet! If it were me, I'd call it off too! A fiancé tangled up with a noodle-selling wench..."

"I heard that Miss Wen has a weak constitution; I'm afraid she can't take this kind of shock..."

Xie Linfeng could no longer stay a moment longer. His normally aloof face was on the verge of cracking apart.

He turned to leave, but was caught by the sleeve by Sanniang: "Young Master Xie... I..."

He violently shook her hand off: "Don't touch me!"

Sanniang stumbled back two steps, her face as pale as paper.

Xie Linfeng strode away without looking back, leaving behind a scene of utter chaos and rumors growing more absurd by the minute.

Xie Linyuan watched his retreating back, a cold sneer hooking the corner of his lips. He turned to the group of aunties and suddenly raised his voice: "Dear aunts, today's events... must, not, be, spread, around, okay~"

"We understand, we understand!" The aunties caught on immediately. "First Young Master Xie, rest assured, our mouths are the tightest! Right, right!"

"Right." "Right." "Right."

"Our mouths are super tight."

"Then many thanks." Xie Linyuan smiled as he cupped his fists. When he turned away, he glanced at Sanniang standing frozen in place; a flash of pity crossed his eyes, but it quickly hardened back into indifference.

---

Imperial Palace · Imperial Study

Old Prince Wen Jing knelt before the imperial throne alongside Wen Qionghua, holding the memorial to annul the marriage high above his head.

"Your Majesty, this old subject implores you to retract the decree and dissolve the engagement between the Wen and Xie families!"

Emperor Xiao Mingqi rubbed his temples, a troubled expression on his face: "Beloved minister, this betrothal was decreed by the late Emperor; how can it be undone just because someone wants to?"

"Your Majesty!" Tears welled in the old prince's fierce eyes. "This old subject has only this one granddaughter, frail since childhood. I only hope she can find a husband who knows how to care for her warmth and cold. But that scoundrel Xie Linfeng is entangled with a common market woman... This old subject simply cannot bear to watch her suffer such grievance!" As he spoke, his voice choked with emotion.

Watching the veteran general who had spent half his life on horseback redden his eyes, the Emperor's heart softened as well.

He looked toward Wen Qionghua standing quietly to the side: "Wen girl, what do you say?" The Empress was on good terms with Wen Qionghua's mother, and Qionghua was someone he had watched grow up. Toward this niece, his voice involuntarily softened.

Qionghua bowed prostrate to the ground: "This subject's daughter implores Your Majesty to grant this."

Her voice was soft yet firm. When she raised her head, the Emperor couldn't help but be startled; the girl's face was as pale as paper, with faint dark bruising under her eyes; clearly, she was seriously ill.

"This body of yours..."

"Replying to Your Majesty, this subject's daughter is fine," Qionghua said softly. "It's just... truly unable to bear such humiliation."

The Emperor pondered for a moment and was about to speak when an urgent eunuch's announcement came from outside the hall:

"Your Majesty! Prime Minister Xie requests an audience!"

"Grant it."

Xie Changlin hurried inside, dropping to his knees the moment he entered: "Your Majesty! This old subject has failed to properly discipline his son; please punish this subject! But the betrothal must not be called off!"

The Old Prince sneered: "Xie Changlin, when your son was publicly humiliating my granddaughter, why didn't I see you stepping out to uphold justice?"

"Your Highness, calm your anger! Linfeng was merely muddle-headed for a moment; this old subject has already disciplined him according to family law! As for that noodle-selling woman, this old subject will make proper arrangements so she never appears in the capital again!"

Hearing this, Wen Qionghua suddenly raised her head: "How does Lord Xie plan to make 'proper arrangements'?"

Xie Yun was startled, clearly not expecting her to suddenly ask.

Wen Qionghua said softly: "Miss Liu committed no wrong; why must Lord Xie make things difficult for her?"

The Old Prince looked at his granddaughter in astonishment.

Qionghua continued: "This subject's daughter requests the annulment not because of Miss Liu, but because since Second Young Master Xie holds no place for this daughter in his heart, forcing this marriage is of no use. I beg Your Majesty to discern the truth."

The Emperor looked at this sickly yet exceptionally clear-headed girl, a trace of appreciation flashing in his eyes. Just as he was about to speak, another announcement came from outside:

"Your Majesty! His Second Highness requests an audience!"

The Emperor furrowed his brows: "What is he here for? Grant audience."

Everyone turned back to see Second Prince Xiao Heng stride in. He wore a dark brocade robe, his features picturesque, a faint, ambiguous smile hanging at the corners of his lips.

"This son pays respects to Royal Father." After offering his greeting, his gaze lingered on Wen Qionghua for a moment before he said with a smile, "This son heard that Miss Wen wishes to call off her engagement, and has come specially to offer a plan."

The Emperor raised an eyebrow: "Oh? What good plan do you have?"

Xiao Heng stood with his hands behind his back, calm and composed: "Since Second Young Master Xie's heart lies elsewhere, why not, bestow Miss Wen upon this son. This son is willing to take Miss Wen as his secondary consort and will surely treat her well..."
